Sports.title: Kayode seals emphatic Brentford victory in wake-up call for sorry Spurs
Sports.content:
Every new season opens with talk of a team winning the transfer window. It is not the same as winning on the pitch and Tottenham found out the hard way after being run out of west London by Brentford, whose dominance made a mockery of suggestions that Spurs are about to take off after casting off the shackles of Levynomics with a summer of relentless spending.

Spurs, whose outlay on new signings will soon surpass £300m, were battered, bruised and embarrassed long before the end. They failed to do the basics against superior opponents and can count themselves fortunate it finished only 3-0 to Brentford, who made light of their inferior resources by opening their second season under Keith Andrews with a dominant win.

Mamadou Sangaré, who looks a bargain after joining from Lens for £39m, was key to an outstanding display from the hosts. The Malian midfielder outshone Sandro Tonali, who became Spurs’ record signing this summer, and is further evidence of Brentford’s canny recruitment.

It will worry Roberto De Zerbi that his side appeared to believe an extravagant transfer window meant they could stroll to victory. Some players chickened out of challenges, others were lazy with their passing and when all the elements of a shocking performance were put together it was not hard to work out why Brentford spent the first half doing as they pleased, to the extent the hosts must have been disappointed they were only 2-0 up at half-time.

Spurs, whose spending in their first summer without Daniel Levy as chair showed their determination not to spend another year listening to taunts about trips to Lincoln, could not have been weaker. They had three new faces in their back four – Andrew Robertson was at left-back while Jan Paul van Hecke partnered Marcos Senesi in the middle – but Brentford found wide open spaces from the start, created havoc with crosses from the wings and had chances to score before the opening goal arrived in the 12th minute.

Sangaré, impressive in Ligue 1 last season, was at the heart of a slick move. The midfielder took possession on the right and encountered little resistance as he drove forward. Spurs merely gawped, nobody reacting as Igor Thiago dropped off to combine with Sangaré, who burst on to the striker’s clever lay-off before cutting the ball back for Keane Lewis-Potter to run in from left-back and beat Antonin Kinsky from close range.

Much is made of Brentford’s threat from set pieces, but this was proof they can be just as effective in open play. Spurs were sliced apart and they continued to ship openings during the early stages. Thiago headed against the bar and Dango Ouattara twice went through on goal, only to take a heavy touch on both occasions.

View image in fullscreen Keane Lewis-Potter fires home Brentford’s opener from close range. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

While Spurs have been busy with their big refurbishment Brentford have benefited from a summer of stability. Sangaré, the one eye-catching addition, was part of a midfield that swamped Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher and Tonali, who did not look £100m well spent. Brentford, so well drilled by Andrews, were rampant. Vitaly Janelt and Mathias Jensen were excellent alongside Sangaré, Kevin Schade tormented Archie Gray on the left and it was not until Brentford were 3-0 up early in the second half that Spurs created a chance of any note.

De Zerbi will hope that bringing in Omar Marmoush and Savinho will add more bite in attack. If only disappointing displays from Richarlison, Mathys Tel and Mikey Moore were the only problem for Spurs, though. There were frailties in every department and the second goal underlined the difference between the sides, Bergvall timid in a challenge with Jensen, Kinsky unable to push the Brentford player’s shot to safety and Janelt quickest to gobble up the rebound.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There were boos from the away end at half-time. De Zerbi reacted, Rodrigo Bentancur replacing the wretched Bergvall and Gallagher’s removal allowing Mateus Fernandes to come on for his debut after his £85m move from West Ham, but Brentford did not need long to stamp out any hope of a fightback.

It was nothing more than a simple corner routine for the hosts to go three ahead in the 49th minute. Nathan Collins was free to nod down at the far post and although Kinsky saved well from Sangaré the ball dropped for Michael Kayode to smash into the roof of the net.

The humiliation was complete and it could have been worse after Bentancur fouled Schade in the area, only for Thiago to hit a post with his penalty.

Sports.title: Carrick tells Manchester United to keep calm and carry on after Hull humbling
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says he will not overreact, but has called for improvement after Manchester United started the season with a 2-0 defeat at Hull. United lost their opening game for the fourth time in the past seven years as Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy took advantage of poor defending from set-pieces.

The United head coach presented a professional exterior despite United’s performance not reaching the desired standard as they were deservedly beaten by Hull, who finished sixth in the Championship last season.

“I’m talking to you quite calmly, but I’m not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day, so there’s a big difference,” he said. “I played [for United] for a long time. You don’t get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, the results, the ups and downs, but you just carry on as normal.

“It’s 100% not that, and trust me, it’s not that. It just doesn’t mean that we all have to shout and scream and come out and create some chaos just because of it. Inside we’re hurting and we need to get better. But the calmness doesn’t mean there’s no emotion in it, for sure.”

He added: “The result’s the result. We got beat, we’re hurt and it’s not a nice feeling. It doesn’t mean it’s going to change the whole direction of how we’re going as a team or as a football club.

“It’s one game and results can happen in football, we all understand that. It’s not nice when they do, but it does happen.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes (left) looks dejected after the match against Hull City Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

United barely threatened throughout the 90 minutes. “Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game,” Bruno Fernandes said. “We gave too much of the ball to them, in the first 20 minutes the goalkeeper had more touches on the ball, too much time. We need to press a little bit more, be more aggressive, and set-plays – we need to work on it, to be more aggressive and try not to concede these types of goals.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hull’s head coach, Sergej Jakirovic, said he and his backroom staff had spotted a weakness in the way United defended set-pieces, but would not divulge his “secret” that helped to expose it.

Hull are strongly tipped for relegation and their supporters sung “are you watching Joe Cole?” during the match after the pundit mocked their chances of survival. “I don’t have any problems with critics with opinions,” Jakirovic said. “We tried to prove them wrong and today we won the game. Now it’s 37 to go, so we will try to continue like this. I’m very, very happy because of all the people in the club.”

Sports.title: Burnham’s boys enjoy visit from Palace as Everton ease to opening day win
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham was in the posh seats to see how his beloved Everton would fare without the key additions that even the prime minister has voiced an opinion on. No right-back, no new centre-forward, no problem: Everton contained enough quality to overcome a wasteful Crystal Palace.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Iliman Ndiaye delivered a timely reminder that, despite the missing pieces in the squad, there is pedigree and Premier League knowhow available to David Moyes as he attempts to sustain a challenge for European qualification this season.

Dewsbury-Hall swept home an outstanding finish to give Everton the lead and sweep away any lingering resentment over how last season flatlined. Ndiaye supplied the superb cross that invited Thierno Barry to seal Everton’s first opening game win since 2021. It was a brutal introduction for the new Palace manager, Pierre Sage, who lost defender Chadi Riad to a potentially serious knee injury late on.

“I spoke to the prime minister on the phone,” Moyes said. “Andy Gray came down into the office [before the game] and his assistant Peter Reid phoned down.”

Reid was Burnham’s chaperone for the day – along with a phalanx of security – and put the prime minister on the phone during his call to Moyes. His good luck message was answered, thanks in part to Palace’s profligacy.

There were no radical changes in formation or personnel from Sage for his first Premier League outing. A lack of cutting edge was familiar from the Oliver Glasner era, too. The visitors created three clear opportunities before Everton took the lead and failed to take any. Misfortune played its part in two of the chances, with Jordan Pickford’s left post struck twice, but that did not diminish the torment for Sage and the travelling support. A sense of the inevitable from Everton increased with each one.

Palace denied reports that Ismaïla Sarr had refused to play because of a desire to join Galatasaray – the Senegal international was absent due to a groin injury, according to his manager – and the disruption had no effect on their start. Eddie Nketiah created an early opportunity for Jean-Philippe Mateta, but his strike partner volleyed over at the near post.

View image in fullscreen Moved from his usual seat into the directors’ box by prime pinisterial security logistics, Andy Burnham celebrated with the Everton legend, and his good friend, Peter Reid. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

Chance number two came from a sublime pass by Adam Wharton, the midfielder who Sage has insisted is going nowhere despite interest from Manchester City. Wharton found Nketiah free inside the area with a perfectly weighted ball over Merlin Röhl, forced to deputise at right-back in the absence of a conclusion to Everton’s almost farcical search for Séamus Coleman’s successor.

Nketiah had time to pick his spot but Pickford produced a superb save to tip the shot on to a post. Mateta struck the same post from another Nketiah cross and Everton took full advantage of their reprieves.

Everton grew into their opening game, with the summer signings Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Röhl all impressing. Creativity was initially in short supply from the home side, despite George’s constant probing on the left, until Dewsbury-Hall and Ndiaye imposed themselves on proceedings.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Dewsbury-Hall’s impact was worth the wait. The midfielder burst into life with a mazy run that ended with an appeal for handball when his shot hit Chris Richards. Play continued through Daniel Muñoz, a possible Everton right-back target, who was dispossessed by the industrious Harrison Armstrong and left a void for Dewsbury-Hall to exploit. Receiving Armstrong’s pass, the 27-year-old swept an unstoppable, angled drive into Dean Henderson’s far corner to open the season in style for Everton.

View image in fullscreen Thierno Barry outjumped Chris Richards to head Everton into a two-goal lead just after half-time. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

Muñoz should have made amends when stealing in ahead of George to meet an inviting delivery from Daichi Kamada. Palace’s end product did not match the buildup yet again, however, and the Colombian defender guided his header wide of the far post.

Everton found the comfort of a two-goal lead when Ndiaye delivered a peach of a cross from the right. Barry, on a self-confessed mission to improve after a difficult debut season in the Premier League, rose between Richards and Jaydee Canvot to head past Henderson at close range. The departure of the unfortunate Riad on a stretcher compounded Palace’s deflating afternoon.

Sports.title: Infantino angers Concacaf nations by hijacking meeting in Caribbean
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has risked alienating numerous Concacaf nations, whose support he is seeking in his re-election campaign, by hijacking a meeting of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU) to announce Fifa-funded development projects for the region with millions of dollars that had been delayed for months.

Multiple sources attending the CFU meeting in the Dominican Republic said many of the Concacaf members were infuriated by Infantino’s behaviour, particularly as he had been asked to stay away by their president, Victor Montagliani.

The Concacaf position echoes previous complaints about Fifa’s operations from the Jordan FA, whose president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, accused Infantino of bribery this month when he claimed they have not received prize money from last year’s Arab Cup due to the country’s failure to endorse the president.

Infantino appears to have seen the CFU meeting as an opportunity to lobby for election votes among Caribbean countries in the hope of causing a split within Concacaf, who have aligned with Uefa and the Asian Football Confederation in demanding his resignation after the World Cup sell-off debacle.

In a letter addressed to Infantino on Friday, Montagliani had asked the Fifa president “in the name of football to reconsider your attendance”, pointing out his presence would take the spotlight away from a regional under-14 tournament being held alongside the meeting.

Despite that entreaty, Infantino is understand to have turned up at the resort of Punta Cana with a large Fifa entourage including the secretary general, Mattias Grafström, and Elkhan Mammadov, a staunch ally who is responsible for maintaining good relations with the 211 members in his role as director of member associations.

Before making funding pledges in the CFU meeting, Infantino’s team are understood to have approached individual member associations lobbying for support. Mammadov has played a central role in attempts to keep them onside since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal broke and his insistent approach has caused disquiet in some quarters.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

One source said the official Fifa party had attempted to portray their governance crisis as a private dispute between Infantino and Montagliani. The Canadian businessman has not commented since news of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise emerged, but has been widely touted in Europe as a possible contender to replace Infantino.

The pair met briefly and shook hands before the CFU meeting in an exchange captured by Infantino’s personal camera crew.

While Mexico, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis have all broken with Concacaf and declared their support for Infantino, the majority of their 41 members are understood to back the alliance with Uefa advocated by Montagliani.

The Uefa/Concacaf pact extends beyond attempts to unseat Infantino, with the two confederations in talks about setting up a joint Nations League in 2028 that could develop further into a new global competition.

Sports.title: Anton Stach snatches late Leeds winner to sour Glasner’s new dawn at Forest
Sports.content:
For Anton Stach, another sweet direct free-kick to add to the back catalogue, this one souring Oliver Glasner’s first match in charge of Nottingham Forest. Only Dominik Szoboszlai eclipsed Stach’s record of three direct free-kick goals in the Premier League last season, one of those coming against Glasner’s Crystal Palace.

Stach’s latest right-foot strike earned Leeds, fresh from a near-flawless pre-season and an expensive and exciting summer in the market, a divine opening-day victory with a couple of minutes of normal time remaining.

It has been a busy few weeks for the Germany midfielder. “He even released a burger a few days ago and I never expected him to do this,” said the Leeds manager, Daniel Farke, alluding to Stach launching a burger at a city-centre eatery to raise money for charity. “He’s a bit of a weird and crazy guy.

“I expected when he was over the free-kick that he could do something special. He has done it time and time again. He surprised me [with his free-kicks] last season [but now] I trust him with everything. Last season, I would have never thought about it.”

For Forest, a few minutes before kick-off, the curtain going up on another season, a new protagonist emerged from the tunnel. Glasner, Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months, surveyed the scene from his technical area. But the start of this new dawn did not go to plan, an underwhelming performance culminating with Stach sneaking in his whipped free-kick at Matz Sels’s near post. At least Forest can put things right quickly, Leeds visiting in a Carabao Cup rematch on Tuesday.

Leeds were imposing and always looked more threatening, rationing Forest to moments. In the first half, Harry Wilson had a debut goal disallowed when the assistant referee raised his flag for offside after the Welshman, whose arrival is evidence of Leeds’ ambition, latched on to Jayden Bogle’s pushed pass. In the second, Sels’ strong left hand prevented a header by the £34m signing Tarik Muharemovic, another debutant, flying into the top corner.

Glasner, who left marquee signing Ousmane Diomande on the bench and introduced Xaver Schlager late on, puffed his cheeks as every outfield Leeds player joined the celebrations. The away end, bathed in the evening sun, was jubilant. The Forest areas began to empty.

“It was pretty clear that I can’t come with my staff, lay our hands on the shoulders [of the players], and all of a sudden we play like Real Madrid in the 70s or whatever,” Glasner said. “It was an OK performance from both teams – a typical first Premier League game after a long break and this is also now not the time to bury our heads into the sand.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Anton Stach jumps for joy after his late winner for Leeds. Photograph: Bruce Rollinson/PA

These remain early days – Nuno Espírito Santo was in charge when Forest beat Brentford in their opening game last season – but they did little to enthuse the locals. Chris Wood arrived from the bench and sent a bobbling ball wide with a first-time shot from Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected pass. Schlager replaced James McAtee for his debut, but Leeds were buoyant at the final whistle.

Only Arsenal and Manchester United scored more set-piece goals than Leeds last season, but Farke dismissed the suggestion they are more important than previously. “There is not one team who won the World Cup without a set-piece goal,” said the German, stating ability from dead balls was a factor in their summer recruitment, Wilson a case in point.

“I remember Germany 12 years ago, a crap [quarter-final] game against France: Mats Hummels header, boom, goal,” he said. “I remember magic free-kick takers: Juninho, who got this crazy curve on the ball. It is always a major part of the game, not just nowadays. Anton is perhaps not as beautiful on the eye like Juninho’s free-kicks, but bloody effective, and I quite like it.”

Sports.title: Enciso shines bright for Ipswich as Emersonn and Clarke sink Sunderland
Sports.content:
It would be fascinating to know which algorithms or eagle-eyed staff in Ipswich’s recruitment department spotted the potential in Emersonn to score the goals to keep them in the Premier League.

Thirteen games, no goals and a serious knee injury at the Brazilian side Athletico Paranaense; two league goals in 17 games at Turkish side Goztepe; then six in 28 at French side Toulouse. A modest return and not one that screams he would be ready to break down doors in the English top flight.

Ipswich have spent more than £150m this summer, determined not to make the same mistakes as the last time they came up. Emersonn became a club record signing – for £24m plus add-ons – beaten a month later by the arrival of the attacking midfielder Julio Enciso for £26m.

In a season of flux and uncertainty, the sparks of a compelling partnership between the pair here offered faint hope Ipswich can stay up against the odds, just as their opponents did last season. They are certainly mirroring Sunderland’s recruitment plan.

“It’s important to assess the gap between the Championship and the Premier League – it’s massive,” the Sunderland manager, Régis Le Bris, said. “They made a good start, which is important, but the consistency throughout the season is a big challenge.”

Enciso and Emersonn combined for the opening goal and regularly tried to find one another. Luke O’Nien, for reasons unbeknown to anyone but himself, had the ball under no pressure on the halfway line but passed straight to Enciso. Anyone watching the previous 23 minutes could see he was the last player you wanted to give the ball to with yards of open grass behind you. Enciso duly skipped past O’Nien, drove into Sunderland’s half, shimmied past Dan Ballard before squaring for Emersonn to scruffily tuck the ball away.

Angulo swept in a marvellous free kick via the crossbar, six minutes before the break, and almost an entire second half of Ipswich pressure looked to be petering out in a draw. But Jack Clarke came on in the 71st minute – replacing man of the match Enciso, who left to a standing ovation – and in the 90th minute he delicately finished into the bottom-right corner.

View image in fullscreen Emersonn takes the plaudits after scoring Ipswich’s first goal against Sunderland. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

“We’ve thrown Emersonn in,” the Ipswich manager, Gary O’Neil, said. “There are still some bits he has to tidy up on. He gave Ballard a tough time, fought him physically.”

There is indubitable flair and talent in the 22-year-old – the first Brazilian to play for Ipswich. Later, with the ball on the left, he evaded Thomas Meunier and Enzo Le Fée by slipping the ball between them, then found Enciso with a low cross, but the attacking midfielder caught the ball wrong.

Enciso has returned to Ipswich as though intent on making up for lost time. He has had nibbles at the Premier League before – first at Brighton, where he could not quite move beyond useful player-to-bring-on, then on loan here the last time Ipswich were in the Premier League, where he impressed as they went down.

He spent a year at Strasbourg under O’Neil, before following the coach back for another crack. “He’s a No 10 who can produce unbelievable quality, but not many 10s in the world are willing to work the way he works,” O’Neil said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I worked hard with him in Strasbourg around his defensive game. He was excellent stopping [Granit] Xhaka dictating. When he beats two players and there’s a shot on goal there’s no thought for himself, he passes to Emersonn. You won’t find many that can do all the sides like him.”

There will be times in retirement when O’Nien will wake up, drenched in sweat, from feverish dreams replaying over and over what Enciso did to him on this afternoon. After a bruising spell, when Enciso darted in to steal the ball from O’Nien’s feet, the defender took a yellow card to avoid being humiliated again.

If it wasn’t O’Nien, it was others. Enciso chopped past Xhaka – the midfielder shaking his head in frustration – then cut inside Nilson Angulo and crossed to the back post, where Emersonn was unable to direct his header on target.

Enciso has the vibe of a diminutive forward capable of producing a world-class performance once every four or five games. If he could find some consistency he could become one of the best players in the league.

Ipswich are back and there is something different about them this time.

Sports.title: Aston Villa upheaval is a risk but Emery can release v2.0 and reap rewards | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Last season was the greatest Aston Villa have enjoyed since they won the European Cup in 1982. They claimed their second European trophy by lifting the Europa League, but even without that would have secured Champions League qualification by finishing fourth in the Premier League.

Despite a miserable start during which they failed to win any of their first five league games, there was even a spell around Christmas when it looked as though Villa might be challengers for the title. The question after a season like that is always: where next?

The answer is probably less clear now than it was amid the delirium of Istanbul in May. A reasonable consideration, even a couple of weeks ago, would have been: was that a one-off high, the limit of the club’s ambitions, or was there more? The danger for any team, but particularly one relatively unfamiliar with success, is to rest on its laurels, to be too loyal to those who have brought the long-awaited silverware.

It’s an understandable enough impulse: any transfer comes with a risk, so why make changes when what was there before worked? Why offload players to whom there is a sense of gratitude? Villa have not rested on their laurels.

Three major players – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa – have left, Emí Martínez seems likely to join them and Ollie Watkins might go as well. This is not a fire sale. Nor is it a club cashing in while it still can. But it probably wasn’t quite planned this way either. The exodus is a combination of accepting that certain players are ready to fly the nest and trying to make as much money from them as possible for a rejuvenation of the squad. The danger is that too much is being changed too quickly.

Those changes have not just been among the playing staff. Two physios and the head of the medical team went to Arsenal. Jaime Arias Galán, a technical assistant, has left. The individual development coach, Rodri, went to Como. Most significantly, Unai Emery’s assistant, Pako Ayestarán, departed, while the set-piece coach, Austin MacPhee, went to Chelsea. There are always changes among backroom staff and the impact is hard for outsiders to assess but, still, the departures add to the sense of flux and uncertainty.

There is logic in the changes to playing personnel, though. Rogers is 24 and had been at the club for two and a half seasons. He scored 14 goals in all competitions in each of the past two seasons, many of them spectacular. He squeezed in the third goal in the Europa League final and will be remembered with great affection by Villa fans but he wanted to go for the better salary and perceived better opportunities (a risk, frankly) at Chelsea.

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi was a flowing sight for Switzerland at the World Cup this summer. Photograph: Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images

Once a player’s mind is set on leaving, there is rarely much point in standing in their way. An Alexander Isak at Newcastle situation helps nobody. Far better to accept the cash and reinvest it. For a player who cost £15m, a fee of £117m, less the 20% owed to Middlesbrough, represents excellent business.

Konsa is 28 but had two years left on his contract. A fee of £51m feels reasonable. Tielemans went after Manchester United triggered his £35m release clause. There was nothing Villa could have done but, given the Belgian is 29, they can at least console themselves that they’re selling a player they picked up on a free in summer 2023 for a reasonable price before any decline has begun. While no club enjoys losing high-class players, trading is a necessary part of squad development – and there is reason to be excited about Villa’s recruitment.

Johan Manzambi is a hugely gifted young attacking midfielder, Zion Suzuki is recognised as one of the most promising young goalkeepers in the world, João Gomes has already shown signs of the tenacity he can bring to the midfield and Matteo Ruggeri probably represents an upgrade on Lucas Digne at left-back. Alejandro Garnacho is a loan signing with potential. The Argentinian winger clearly has talent; the issue is releasing it consistently. Aaron Wan-Bissaka, reliable cover at right-back, has joined from relegated West Ham.

And all that with a net surplus of £160m, plus whatever they may get for Watkins should he leave. More signings will arrive. There is need of a defender to replace Konsa. Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson represents an obvious option to replace Watkins, given his capacity to exploit the space behind opposing defensive lines. The thought of him and Manzambi linking with Brian Madjo, the 17-year-old centre-forward who made such an impression in the Uefa Super Cup defeat by Paris Saint-Germain, is undeniably enticing.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another central midfielder looks essential, particularly after Amadou Onana tore his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup. There will probably be at least one and possible two more creative players, one to operate centrally and one in the left.

View image in fullscreen Villa’s teenage forward Brian Madjo gave Paris Saint-German a torrid time in this month’s Super Cup. Photograph: Joao Bravo/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

That means potentially seven or eight major arrivals over the summer, and that is a lot. It hasn’t always been easy for new signings to adapt themselves to Emery’s methods. The Spaniard has insisted there are “six or seven contenders” who are better equipped than Villa this season.

Managers habitually try to play down expectation and, given the changes, it’s understandable Emery should take that stance. It may even be accurate. But it’s also true that a lot of sides have undergone a lot of change this season – and Villa at least have retained the same manager.

It may even be that this is a necessary stage of development, of rejuvenation and of the accumulation of capital before a renewed assault on the heights. Certainly the shift from Profitability and Sustainability Rules to squad cost ratio should suit Villa. But in an ideal world, all three of Rogers, Konsa and Tielemans would not have gone in the same summer; to undergo this much change at once is an enormous risk.

It is, though, risk with a potential upside, whereas sitting back and relishing the memory of last season would have led inevitably to decline. One phase is ending, a new one beginning and, while it might go wrong, Emery 2.0 may, in time, be even better for Villa than the first version.

Sports.title: European football: Inter start title defence with rout of promoted Monza
Sports.content:
Inter kicked off their ⁠Serie A title defence with a 4-1 home win over ⁠Monza, ​after the promoted side recovered from conceding an early ⁠goal to go in level at the break before the ⁠champions turned on the style.

Hakan Calhanoglu ​put Inter ahead ‌in the ‌sixth minute, but the hosts were ‌far too complacent after taking the lead and Gustavo Varela equalised for the visitors just before the half-hour.

Inter began the second half as ‌they had the first, with Piotr Zielinski scoring three minutes ​after the break, before Pio Esposito and Yann Bisseck wrapped up the win for Cristian Chivu’s side.

The England defender ⁠John Stones came on to make ​his ​Inter debut, with ​compatriots and fellow recent signings ​Djed Spence ‌and Curtis ​Jones ​watching on at San Siro.

View image in fullscreen John Stones (right) makes his debut for Inter Milan. Photograph: Francesco Scaccianoce/Inter/Getty Images

Udinese drew 1-1 at home to Como in the other early game. Last season’s runners-up, Napoli, visit Genoa later on Saturday.

The Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said his new signing Rodri would not be involved in the Spanish champions’ La Liga opener against Elche on Sunday. The former Manchester City midfielder may, however, be able to take part in their second match, against Athletic Bilbao, on Thursday. “He’s very concentrated, focused, our plan is that he will arrive on Monday with the team,” Flick said on Saturday. “This is the plan. He’s a fantastic player, a leader, and his personality is very great.”

Real Madrid’s season opener is later on Saturday, with José Mourinho’s second spell in charge starting at Espanyol.

Last weekend, Dino Toppmöller won his first competitive game in charge of Lens, beating PSG in the French Champions Trophy.

Auxerre had the defender Christ Makosso sent off in the first half for a foul on the Lens attacker Abdallah Sima.

Sports.title: Jean-Philippe Mateta goes to war with Crystal Palace: Wantaway striker takes his club to FIFA over claims the final months of his contract should be void
Sports.content:
Jean-Philippe Mateta goes to war with Crystal Palace: Wantaway striker takes his club to FIFA over claims the final months of his contract should be void

Jean-Philippe Mateta is arguing that the final months of his Crystal Palace contract are invalid and has taken his challenge to FIFA.

Palace activated the option year in Mateta's contract in 2024 and his current deal is due to expire at the end of this season.

But the 29-year-old is arguing that the contract should be void and that he should have been a free agent this summer.

Mateta's case was heard by an independent tribunal under the Premier League's rules and he subsequently went to FIFA, but they ruled earlier this week that overruling the contract is not within their jurisdiction.

Jean-Philippe Mateta is arguing that the final months of his Crystal Palace contract are invalid

Palace this week rebuffed an enquiry from Aston Villa for Mateta and more clubs are expected to try in the final days of the window.

Mateta, who started Palace's Premier League opener at Everton on Saturday, signed for the club from Mainz 05, initially on an 18-month loan.

He signed a four-and-a-half year contract when joining permanently in January 2022, in a deal that also included the option of a 12-month extension.

Sports.title: Brentford 3-0 Tottenham: This was as comprehensive as defeats come. Roberto De Zerbi's men were outplayed and unable to cope with their slick hosts, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Brentford 3-0 Tottenham: This was as comprehensive as defeats come. Roberto De Zerbi's men were outplayed and unable to cope with their slick hosts, writes MATT BARLOW

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Amid so much change, some things remain the same. And there is still nothing quite like a trip to Brentford in the Premier League to bring the lofty expectations of the self-appointed elite crashing back to earth.

Tottenham, having escaped the ignominy of relegation, settled upon a head coach to their liking and spent a couple of hundred million in the transfer market, took a hiding at the hands of the Bees and should be flattered by the scoreline.

Roberto De Zerbi saw his team outplayed in every department. Unable to cope with the intensity and physicality in midfield. Unable to handle Brentford's aerial presence up at the back. Unable to get a hold of the ball and offer any threat in attack

This was as comprehensive as defeats come. Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode scored the goals, and Igor Thiago missed a penalty.

Spurs barely stirred. Apart from a late effort by Mikey Moore, superbly saved by Caoimhin Kelleher, they did not look like scoring. Perhaps most worrying of all, they appeared reluctant to engage in the battle they faced.

De Zerbi might add Savinho and Omar Marmoush next week and but there is still work to be done on the fundamentals of competing at this level, what he called 'the soul of the team' on the eve of this season.

Roberto De Zerbi cut a forlorn figure as Tottenham sank to a 3-0 defeat opening-day defeat at Brentford

The Italian cut a forlorn figure on the touchline with hands in pockets as the jubilant home crowd taunted him with songs about Thomas Frank, relegation and wasted money.

Brentford, we should note, were excellent. Slick and cohesive. They know what they are and what they are trying to achieve and in Mamadou Sangare had the most influential of all the big-money summer singings on display.

Sangare, signed for a club record £41million from Lens, eclipsed £100m Sandro Tonali. In the second half, he eclipsed £85m Mateus Fernandes, too. The new central defensive pairing Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi had no answer for the aerial assault led by Thiago.

The Bees, having been written off following a summer upheaval last year, have basked in a summer of serenity this year under Keith Andrews. They scored seven on their final pre-season outing against Eintracht Frankfurt and were again in fluent attacking mood again.

Sangare created the opening goal, carrying the ball forward, bouncing a one-two off Thiago and cutting a low cross square for Lewis-Potter to convert.

Lewis-Potter has matured into an excellent left back. His strength is going forward but he has become capable in defence and deceptively strong in the air. He had already seen one sweet volley blocked from a corner and Nathan Collins had turned a good chance wide with a near post header. Thiago headed another against the bar but there was a flag up for offside.

James Maddison and his Tottenham team-mates applaud the fans after this bruising defeat

Keane Lewis-Potter put Brentford in just the 12th minute as they made a fast start on Saturday

Home fans were buoyant. Thrilled by the attacking vibrancy of their own team and perhaps enjoying further disorder in the ranks of the visitors on behalf of Frank, their popular former boss who was given short shrift when he left for Spurs.

When the teams met here on New Year's Day, the 0-0 draw unfolded to the stinging soundtrack of 'Boring Boring Tottenham' from the away end. It proved the beginning of the end for Frank, sacked 41 days later with relegation fears taking a grip.

De Zerbi's rescue mission lifted spirits, and investment in new players fuelled hope of a better season ahead. The Spurs boss named four debutants to start. Fernandes from the bench made it five. They were led out by Archie Gray, the club's youngest captain the club in a competitive match at 20 years, 163 days but it was not an occasion he will cherish.

Subbed before the end, Gray was serenaded by Bees supporters who have not forgotten he snubbed them for Spurs. 'Should've signed for a big club,' they crowed.

Janelt scored Brentford's second before the interval. Mathias Jensen beat Lucas Bergvall in a tackle and tested goalkeeper Toni Kinsky with a skidding shot from the edge of the penalty area.

Kinsky made a mess of the save and spilled it into a dangerous area, and Janelt was quickest to the rebound, an all-encompassing defensive shambles with familiar echoes for Spurs.

Brentford's new £41m signing Mamadou Sangare played a starring role against Tottenham

Going forward, they offered very little. Mathys Tel had a tame free kick easily gathered by Kelleher and Tonali lashed a hopeful shot over from distance and high into the top tier of the stand and greeted by chants of, 'what a waste of money'.

De Zerbi's made half-time changes to his midfield. Off came Bergvall and Conor Gallagher. On came Fernandes and Rodrigo Bentancur. It gave them a little more control but not before Brentford grabbed a third via a smooth corner routine.

Collins, unmarked in the deep, headed the ball down to Sangare's whose fierce strike from the edge of the penalty box was saved by Kinsky. Michael Kayode pounced to fire the loose ball high into the net.

From the Spurs angle, there were maddening similarities to the previous goal. Bees were first to the header, first to the knock-down and first to the rebound. They should have made it 4-0 from the spot when Bentancur was ruled by referee Michael Oliver to have pushed on Kevin Schade.

Thiago hit a post having sent Kinsky the wrong way. It was perhaps the only real mistake made by Brentford. Alas, for Spurs there were many.

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba to undergo Man United medical TODAY as Crystal Palace slap down Jean-Philippe Mateta enquiry and Aston Villa agree terms with free agent Leon Goretzka: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa agree terms for Goretzka

Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.

Pending a medical, the 31-year-old is expected to sign a three-year deal this week.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis was left out of Southampton's squad to face Stoke City amid Villa's interest in the defender.

Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer

Villa have had an enquiry for Jean-Philippe Mateta knocked back by Crystal Palace.

Unai Emery's team are hunting a centre-forward with Al-Hilal pushing hard to sign Ollie Watkins.

Villa are also ready to bid for Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea. Watkins has also been offered a new deal at Villa.

Napoli sign Chelsea star on loan

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy.

The loan fee is worth £2.5million and could rise to £3.4m with add-ons. The option price is around £23m.

Chelsea could receive more than £26m from the deal if Badiashile moves permanently. They valued him at £30m in this window.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy

Napoli are also one of the clubs keen on Chelsea's Marc Guiu. He is weighing up options from Spain and Germany too.

Hull City are exploring a loan for Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo who is also wanted at Strasbourg.

Wrexham eye up move for Millwall's Azeez

Wrexham are exploring a move for Millwall forward Femi Azeez.

The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City.

The Robins are hoping the Nigeria international will be attracted by their ambitious project despite Millwall being rival promotion contenders.

Wrexham are also looking at Ipswich Town attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti.

The 25-year-old Albania international only joined in January from Bristol City for £3.5m and scored his first goal for the club against Wrexham.

The move would mean him giving up the opportunity of Premier League football now though Wrexham hope to be there in a year's time.

Meanwhile, Wrexham's move for free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe looks to be off.

The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City

Brighton enquire about Hull target Hernandez

Brighton have asked about Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez.

The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also.

Hull owner Acun Ilicali said: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself.

'This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. He is young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.'

Brighton remain in talks with Liverpool over the sale of winger Yankuba Minteh.

Though the 22-year-old wants the move, the clubs are some distance apart on valuation with Brighton wanting over £70m to reflect market prices.

The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also

Blues keep tabs on Conceicao amid interest in Neto

Juventus winger Francisco Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto.

Conceicao was bought from Porto for £36million and Juventus would want some profit on their outlay for the 23-year-old Portugal international.

Neto has interest from Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea are asking £100m.

They also have an offer from Roma for Jamie Gittens but so far that's too low, as a loan with option.

Conceicao is quick, technically good and robust for his diminutive stature.

Juventus would look to utilise any money from Conceicao for targets such as Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee.

Juventus winger Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto, with Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City all interested in Neto

Magpies reignite interest in Spurs' Gray

Newcastle United have rekindled interest in Tottenham's versatile midfielder Archie Gray.

The 20-year-old is still very much part of coach Roberto de Zerbi's plans as he can cover various positions though midfield is his preference. He has also captained the team during pre-season.

Newcastle are speaking to Manchester City about Nico Gonzalez but Gray is also someone they admire.

After losing so much quality they are exploring a number of options to strengthen their squad and add Premier League experience.

Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield.

Tottenham will need to consider sales to offset their substantial summer spending, though they would prefer to sell others. Gray is valued over £60m.

Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield and has captained the side during pre-season

Joao Pedro signs eight-year Blues contract

Joao Pedro has signed his new Chelsea contract until 2034.

Chelsea have been determined to keep the Brazil international after he emerged as a target for Barcelona early in the summer.

The Brazil international joined the Blues from Brighton in July 2025 and made an immediate impact, scoring in the Club World Cup semi-final and final as Chelsea were crowned world champions.

His form continued into his first full season at Stamford Bridge, with the forward scoring 20 goals in all competitions.

While the club are willing to listen to offers for Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, the 24-year-old was named Chelsea's new No 9 last week.

Joao Pedro said: 'I am very happy to sign a new contract with Chelsea. I always dreamed of playing for a big club, and it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club.

'Everyone is very excited for this season. We know we can achieve a lot of things. We have a great team, we have a coach who wants to win and has won already.'

Joao Pedro, who has signed a fresh eight-year deal at Chelsea, said: 'I always dreamed of playing for a big club, it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club'

Baleba prepares for Man United medical

Carlos Baleba is due to undergo his medical today ahead of completing his £70million move from Brighton to Manchester United.

The 22-year-old is recovering from an ankle ligament injury but is expected to be fit towards the end of next month.

The deal was agreed early on Friday evening at £65m plus add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Newcastle target given the green light for move

Gonzalez was ready to fight for his place but with City looking to sign two more midfielders they are realistic about his prospects of playing regularly.

Newcastle believe he is open to the move and is emerging as their priority on a shortlist of three targets.

Nico Gonzalez has been told that he can move from Man City amid interest from Newcastle

Man City's talks for Ayyoub Bouaddi are continuing, though Lille have been pushing for optimum price on the 18-year-old.

Man City forward Omar Marmoush is still expected to complete his move to Tottenham.

Liverpool fledgling books Levente loan deal

Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is joining Levante on loan.

The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England as yet, so is having to be loaned out to play competitive football.

The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future.

First team football in a top league such as LaLiga is viewed as an integral next step.

He has travelled to Valencia to complete terms. Ndukwe also had interest from clubs in Portugal, France and Germany.
