Sports.title: Man United's two major areas of concern, the four players who failed to shine in Michael Carrick's system but why there is still no need for panic, writes NATHAN SALT
Sports.content:
Hull City, by their own admission, watched Manchester United three times in the lead up to this lunchtime clash.

Of those three scouting missions - which included a 4-2 drubbing at the hands of AC Milan - only one saw them view it live. That was all Sergej Jakirovic and his staff needed to devise a plan that would ruthlessly expose the flaws in United's plan.

What they found, particularly against Milan, was a system which left huge gaps in the full-back areas to exploit. Set pieces were also viewed as a major area of weakness.

It is a system that pushed Luke Shaw extremely high up the pitch from left back. It is a system that pushed Patrick Dorgu into a clogged central area. A system that asked too much from Noussair Mazraoui. A system that had Matheus Cunha in a floating central role. A system that delivered, in captain Bruno Fernandes' opinion, the same, old mistakes.

'We watched Man United three times, one time live. We saw their problems and then we tried to use this today,' the Hull City boss explained.

'Everything that we agreed on in the meeting this week, everything that we tried to practice went as planned, and this is the result in the end. I'm very, very pleased with them.'

There is credence to what Michael Carrick says. This is one game. One defeat. A bad one, yes. But one defeat. You don't abandon an entire methodology after one bad performance.

But even the most optimistic United fan would concede that pace, or lack thereof, and predictability are two areas of genuine concern for a United side that have too much talent to be this lacklustre on a regular basis.

Luke Shaw was among the players who struggled as Man United were beaten by Hull City

Take the two goals. The first finished off by Semi Ajayi but a goal borne out of Regan Slater's corner, flicked on by John Egan and the chaos that followed, thanks to Oli McBurnie brushing off Ayden Heaven, left United all at sea.

In that sequence, Harry Maguire ended up tangled with his own team-mate in Mazraoui as Ajayi peeled off them both. Neither will reflect on that with any satisfaction.

The second, headed in by Nobel Mendy, saw Slater's wide free kick punish another area that, 24 hours out from the game, a pow-wow on Hull City's training ground explained would be another notable area of weakness for Carrick's side.

Hull City's coaches held court at the training ground on Friday to map out to players exactly how to expose Manchester United from set-pieces.

Particularly, it would later be explained, from wide free kicks.

So here, when Regan Slater lined up a free kick that was headed in by Nobel Mendy to make it 2-0 and land the knockout blow on a hapless Manchester United side that left battered and bruised.

'I don't have a coach for set pieces,' Jakirovic beamed. 'So Marko (Salatovic), Anđelo (Roguljic), my assistant coach, and owner, they are doing this. This is our secret!

'We tried something on Friday, so we had some plan there to try to punish them, how they're standing, especially on the wide free kicks to make some blocks there, and then we saw Nobel and Semi score.'

Bruno Fernandes looks dejected as he makes his way off the pitch after his side lost 2-0

Even outside of set pieces, make no mistake that Hull City bullied Manchester United here. They were quicker, more inventive, braver in and out of possession, and they ultimately had the better game-plan.

'Man United is coming very high with (left back) Luke Shaw,' explained Jakirovic. 'Also, they're trying to overload midfield.

'That was our main task, to close these gaps between the lines.

'When we steal the ball, we are very vertical, very quick. Also, in those transitions, we tried to switch the side because our wing-backs are completely alone.

'We have numbers in the box. We had, I think, two very good chances after this. Also, we didn't allow any one-to-one or 100 per cent chance for Man United.'

They exploited all of that. None of the changes, which included Marcus Rashford's first competitive appearance for United since 2024, nor bringing on an orthodox centre forward in Sesko, improved things.

There were many green shoots of life for United in pre-season: a press that looked capable of suffocating the very best teams, rotations that suggested there would not be an over-reliance on the magic of Bruno Fernandes, and a dominance against the likes of Atletico Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain that suggested a shift was incoming.

Leny Yoro mentioned a possible title tilt. Carrick, albeit optimistic, looked to keep things in check during the summer but did go as far as to say his side has the capability to 'do something special'.

Yes, there is Amad to come back into the group. There's Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt. There's Mason Mount. Benjamin Sesko only came off the bench here. Carlos Baleba will arrive in a £70million deal and a left back is expected.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada could only watch on and wince as they watched this horror showing unfold. More players may yet come through the door amid interest in Joshua Zirkzee between now and the deadline.

But here was the blueprint to beat Manchester United for anyone keen enough to read it.

If one set-piece training session and one live scouting mission is all it takes to unpick an entire tactical game-plan, perhaps keeping calm and carrying on may not be the best course of action after all.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold opens up on abuse after acrimonious Liverpool departure, admitting it 'hurts' as he hopes for 'understanding' from fans over his move to Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold opens up on abuse after acrimonious Liverpool departure, admitting it 'hurts' as he hopes for 'understanding' from fans over his move to Real Madrid

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Trent Alexander-Arnold has expressed hope Liverpool fans will one day understand his decision to join Real Madrid, after admitting he has been 'hurt' by abuse received following the move.

Alexander-Arnold joined the Spanish giants in the summer of 2025, with the Liverpool academy graduate signing a six-year deal.

The full back's departure had caused a backlash from the Liverpool fanbase, with many angry that he had let his contract run down, preventing the club from garnering a significant fee.

Alexander-Arnold ultimately completed a £10million move with Real Madrid opting to sign him ahead of the FIFA Club World Cup.

The 27-year-old has now opened up on abuse he received following the move, including on social media.

Prior to his return to Anfield last season for a Champions League tie, a mural dedicated to Alexander-Arnold had also been defaced with the words 'adios el rata' (Spanish for 'goodbye rat').

Trent Alexander-Arnold suffered jeers on his return to Liverpool last season with Real Madrid

The full back admits the abuse following his move to Real Madrid 'hurts', including seeing a mural in his honour vandalised with the word 'rat'

'Abuse online and threats made via social DMs or in other ways are a sad part of life in 2026 if you're in the public eye and doing things that create a lot of attention. I choose to keep those things away from me because they don't feel real,' Alexander-Arnold told the Daily Mirror.

'I can rationalise that by knowing it's not representative of a football club I love, Liverpool, and it's not representative of my home city.'

Alexander-Arnold had been booed on his return to Anfield, when the full back was introduced as a substitute.

The Real Madrid star admitted he could understand the reception but expressed hope Liverpool fans will become more understanding in time.

'The booing and disappointment from Liverpool supporters is something I'm absolutely able to shoulder. I can understand it, in my own way,' Alexander-Arnold added.

'I heard a lot during that period that Liverpool fans didn't want to be told how to feel or think, and I agree. But I hope one day there'll be a degree of understanding about the decisions I wanted to make around my own life.

'It hurts because of how much I've put into the club over the course of 20 years and the sacrifices I made for the club during that period.

Alexander-Arnold, who enjoyed a trophy laden spell at Liverpool, expressed hope fans will understand his decision in time

'So of course it hurts, but I understand the disappointment. I even understand anger expressed through booing.'

Alexander-Arnold enjoyed stunning success during his time at Liverpool, helping the club to win two Premier League titles and the Champions League in 2019.

The Reds also won the FA Cup, two Carabao Cups, the UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup during his long spell at the club.

Alexander-Arnold had a mixed debut campaign with Real Madrid last season, with the Spanish giants finishing trophyless for the second successive campaign.

The full back made 35 appearances during a season which was disrupted by a series of injuries.

Sports.title: Quevin Castro dead at 25: Former West Brom footballer dies after collapsing during a friendly in Portugal as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
A former West Bromwich footballer has died aged just 25.

Quevin Castro, who grew up in Thetford in Norfolk where he attended the local secondary school, collapsed during a friendly match with third-tier Portuguese side Real Sport Clube.

Desperate attempts were made to revive him with a defibrillator by a doctor with the top-flight team he was playing against, Estrela da Amadora, which is based in Amadora just north-west of Lisbon.

He was rushed to hospital but pronounced dead shortly after arrival.

The tragedy happened earlier today.

West Brom fan page westbrom.fc said this afternoon alongside a photo of Portuguese-born Quevin: 'Former West Bromwich Albion player Quevin Castro has passed away aged 25.

Former West Brom footballer Quevin Castro has died at the age of 25 after collapsing in a friendly

'Our thoughts and prayers go out to his friends and family during this extremely difficult time. RIP, Quevin.'

A supporter reacted by saying: 'RIP Quevin. What a shock. Condolences to the family.'

Another said: 'Wow, aged 25. Gone playing the sport he loved. Horrible news. May he rest in peace.'

Another added: 'That's devastating. Far too young. RIP.'

The central midfielder, whose full name was Quevin Moises Cachicote da Rocha de Castro, had turned 25 on August 16.

He moved back to his homeland from Isthmian League Premier Division club Eastbourne Borough.

He played non-league football for Mildenhall Town, Thetford Town, Norwich CBS, Leiston and Bury Town during his early career.

Castro had trial spells at Ipswich Town in 2019 and later in 2020, and also spent time on trial at Sutton United, Arsenal, Chelsea and West Bromwich Albion.

In the summer of 2021, Castro signed for West Brom on a two-year contract following his trial at the club.

Real Sport Clube paid tribute to Castro on social media following his tragic death

He made his debut for the club on August 25, 2021, starting in a 6-0 EFL Cup second round defeat to Arsenal.

He went on to make his only league appearance for West Brom on February 28, 2022, as a substitute in a 2-0 Championship defeat to Swansea City

On July 14, 2022, Castro joined League One side Burton Albion on a season-long loan.

Castro had his loan terminated by mutual consent on September 1 of that year and later joined National League club Notts County on loan.

He went on to play for a number of clubs including King's Lynn and Chippenham Town before signing for Eastbourne Borough in March this year.

Today's match was cancelled following the footballer's collapse.

The footballer collapsed in the tenth minute of the match.

Estrela da Amadora said in a statement on its website, referencing Quevin's current club by the name Real Massama as it is commonly known although its formal name is Real Sport Clube: 'Estrela da Amadora hereby expresses its profound sorrow at the passing of Quévin Castro, player of Real Massamá.

'In this moment of profound sadness, Estrela da Amadora extends its deepest condolences to the family and friends of Quévin Castro, as well as to the entire Real Massama organization.

'Our thoughts are with all those who were close to him.

'Rest in peace, Quevin.'

Real Sport Clube said alongside a black ribbon photo and Quevin's name underneath: 'It is with profound sadness and great sorrow that Real Sport Clube announces the passing of Quevin Castro, a player and beloved member of our sporting family.

'Quevin Castro was far more than a player, he was a member of our family, leaving a mark on all those who had the privilege of knowing him, both on and off the pitch.

'At this time of grief, Real Sport Clube extends its most sincere condolences to the family and all friends of Quevin Castro, expressing its full solidarity and unconditional support.

'May the memory of Quevin Castro live on in our hearts.

'Rest in peace.'

Sports.title: Everton claim 2-0 win over Crystal Palace, Premier League new boys Ipswich stun Sunderland and Leeds leave it late against Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Everton claim 2-0 win over Crystal Palace, Premier League new boys Ipswich stun Sunderland and Leeds leave it late against Nottingham Forest

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Andy Burnham grew up watching an Everton legend called Kevin Sheedy conjure up goals with a left foot that appeared to be sprinkled with magic dust. So the Prime Minister would have appreciated more than most the strike by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall that put his favourite team on the path to victory.

The Merseysiders had been second best in a first half packed with chances when Dewsbury-Hall took aim just inside the angle of Crystal Palace's penalty area. The crispness of the connection with his left boot was pure Sheedy.

The ball exploded past Palace keeper Dean Henderson in a blur - and David Moyes' team didn't look back.

Burnham was ensconced next to his wife Frankie and boyhood hero Peter Reid in the best seats in the house. He resisted the temptation to wear a replica shirt, but his royal blue suit gave the game away.

He was on his feet again when a close-range header by Thierno Barry early in the second half persuaded Palace that this wasn't going to be their day.

'I spoke to the Prime Minister on the phone before the game when Andy Gray came into my office,' said Everton manager David Moyes. 'He was with his assistant, Peter Reid!

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was on target as Everton claimed all three points against Crystal Palace

'I think it's the first time in five years since we've won on the opening day. Kiernan's goal was very good - but we also needed our goalkeeper. After we scored the second goal we probably should have gone on to score one or two more.'

New Palace manager Pierre Sage has inherited a seasoned squad that had won the Europa Conference League just 89 days earlier. For the first 41 minutes, the game appeared to be theirs for the taking, with Adam Wharton running the show.

But missed chances - and the intervention of inspired Everton keeper Jordan Pickford - took their toll.

Jean-Philippe Mateta fired an early opening over and Daniel Munoz was denied by Pickford before the Everton keeper excelled himself to tip Eddie Nketiah's close-range effort against the post after Wharton had illustrated why Manchester City have told the London club to name their price with a delicious lofted pass.

When Mateta then beat Pickford with a side-footed shot from Nketiah's cross, only to see the ball rebound back off the same post, it seemed inevitable there would be a reckoning.

'Sometimes in football, you don't score when you deserve to score - and you pay the bill,' lamented Sage. 'You have to convert your chances.'

Everton had also created chances during an opening half that was so end-to-end it would have driven both Sage and Everton manager David Moyes to distraction, with Iliman Ndiaye first thumping a shot straight at Henderson when given a clear sight of goal from 12 yards and later dragging another decent opportunity wide.

Moyes had spent the build-up to the game suggesting chief executive Angus Kinnear had been mistaken to suggest that Everton's failure to qualify for Europe last season represented failure.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham celebrates alongside Everton legend Peter Reid in the stands

His team were transformed by Dewsbury-Hall's opening goal, which came about thanks to the tenacity of homegrown teenager Harrison Armstrong.

When Merlin Rohl's quick free kick on the right flank in the 53rd minute caught Palace napping, the outstanding Ndiaye punished them with a cross that took Henderson out of the equation and Barry couldn't miss from inside the six-yard box.

Ndiaye forced Henderson into another save before Tyrique George blazed a chance over as the visitors could barely raise a riposte.

Palace missed the injured Ismaila Sarr, with Sage confirming that the Senegalese forward's absence wasn't down to interest from Galatasaray. 'Sarr will be training on Monday,' said Sage. 'He has a contract and he has won many trophies with us.'

BY SIMON MULLOCK

Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland

Jack Clarke scored a dramatic late winner to get newly-promoted Ipswich off to the perfect start on their Premier League return against Sunderland.

Former Black Cats winger Clarke came off the bench to raise the roof off Portman Road with a 90th-minute strike to hand Gary O'Neil the dream start to life as Tractor Boys boss.

Ipswich only won one home game all season during their last Premier League campaign two years ago but have already matched that this term with a memorable victory on the opening weekend.

Perhaps inspired by their opening day opponents, who finished seventh in the top flight last year, O'Neil handed out six full debuts after spending £150 million so far this summer in an attempt to bridge the gap.

'I thought we played pretty well,' the Ipswich boss said. 'I thought we deserved to win on the balance of it. New signings and players that have been here a while, all pulling together.

'The players know that they can compete at the level. We were competitive today in all phases. I'm 100 per cent confident that they will give everything in every game and we will find a way to be competitive.

'The most confident that I've been in a group that I know what I'm going to see, and I know that they're going to give everything.'

Powerful striker Brian Brobbey was the first to threaten, but Ipswich left-back Leif Davis was on hand to snuff out the danger with an important late block after Trai Hume's forward pass.

Jack Clarke scored a dramatic late winner to get newly-promoted Ipswich off to the perfect start

Club record signing Emersonn had the hosts' first sight of goal soon after, using his status as a target man to good effect as his header was almost fumbled by Robin Roefs.

Ipswich's big moment came after 24 minutes when Emersonn lifted the roof off Portman Road, scoring the game's opening goal after fine work from Julio Enciso on his own second Town debut.

Enciso, who only joined from Strasbourg on Monday, pounced on a loose pass and burst past both Luke O'Nien and Dan Ballard after winning possession inside his own half.

From there, the Paraguay international unselfishly laid off for the onrushing Emersonn to finish into the empty net on his maiden Ipswich appearance.

Dutch goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen was forced into a strong stop to deny compatriot Brobbey's powerful header on goal as the visitors sought an immediate response.

They got it shortly before half-time when a wonderful free-kick from Nilson Angulo found the net moments after Enciso had fired over at the other end.

From 25 yards out, Angulo curled into the top corner via the underside of the crossbar. Even the long arms of 6ft 9in keeper Scherpen, the Premier League's tallest ever player, could not keep it out.

'Welcome back to the Premier League, someone smashes one into the top corner from 25 yards and it's back to square one,' O'Neil said afterwards.

Enciso worked some magic shortly after half-time and almost scored a stunner, with his inventive hook round the corner just evading the far post with Roefs stranded.

Almost immediately at the other end, Brobbey came close to giving Sunderland the lead when pouncing on an Ipswich error, but Marcelino Nunez was well-placed to block.

The energetic Enciso was showing his class and created another chance soon after, but Daizen Maeda was unable to meet Emersonn's headed cutback around the penalty spot.

As Ipswich began to tire, O'Neil threw on last season's top scorer Clarke in an attempt to swing momentum back in their favour, a decision that paid its dividends.

Sasa Lukic, another of Town's experienced summer arrivals, pounced on Omar Alderete's loose pass and allowed Clarke to do the rest on the edge of the box.

The Tractor Boys' super sub curled into the far corner beyond Roefs to lift the noise levels and hand Ipswich the best possible start to their latest top flight campaign.

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris rued: 'At the minute, we are not clinical enough to create chances and score goals. They enjoyed using those opportunities.

'We were in control when we made those mistakes. We'll learn from that experience. It was the problem of the afternoon and we didn't solve it.

'When you make mistakes, you get punished. It's not new. We want to get better and we'll bounce back.'

BY KALLUM BRISSET

Nottingham Forest 0-1 Leeds

So much for Nottingham Forest's bright new dawn under Oliver Glasner. If the Austrian is to have the same transformative effect as he did at Crystal Palace, he will need to find much more than this. He will need some more players for a start.

Forest didn't deserve to lose this dreadful opening-day affair at the City Ground, but they certainly didn't do anywhere near enough to win it. Neither, in all honesty, did Leeds. The fairest of all outcomes would have been for both teams to shake hands, go home with a point apiece, and agree to forget the previous turgid two hours ever happened.

Maybe it was the early-season rust. Glasner described it as a 'typical first Premier League game'. Maybe it was two rusty teams playing the same three-at-the-back system finding themselves at an impasse.

This is only the first match, of course, but either way these two clubs who spent most of last season fighting against relegation showed little to suggest they won't have to scrap again. We can only hope their League Cup clash here again on Tuesday is more exciting.

Another set-piece season?

It was fitting, in the end, that this contest should be decided at the death by a set-piece as Anton Stach curled a free-kick from the edge of the penalty area past a flapping, bewildered Matz Sels. All of the best chances came from dead balls, whether it be corners or long throws, with so little of anything resembling quality emerging from open play.

Anton Stach curled a free-kick from the edge of the penalty area to earn Leeds three points at Nottingham Forest

Leeds, and Stach, are becoming masters of them. Glasner told his players that whoever won the set piece battle would win the match. It was such a huge part of the Premier League last season, the early signs are that it could be again.

'We are talking so much about set-pieces being so important nowadays,' said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. 'Even in my day, set pieces were important. Remember magic free-kick taker Juninho, curling the ball. If you want to be successful, if you want to win the title one day, you have to be good at set pieces. Anton is maybe not as beautiful on the eye as Juninho's free kicks but effective!'

Forest struggle to fill Anderson void

No new signings started for Forest and it showed. There was always going to be an Elliot Anderson-shaped hole in Nottingham Forest's midfield following his £116million move to Manchester City, the question was how Glasner would fill it.

Instead of combative new signing Xaver Schlager, Glasner went for precision and artistry of James McAtee. The midfielder struggled in his first season at Forest after his £30m move from Manchester City but there's hope that under Glasner, he can thrive playing in the same quarter-back role as Adam Wharton did for him at Palace.

As tackles and fouls flew around, McAtee at least tried to bring some decorum. There was a neat little backheel flick to Morgan Gibbs-White that drew a rare oooh of excitement and it was his cross into the box that found the head of Nikola Milenkovic, whose effort struck the post.

Yet it was just moments. It was not enough for Forest to dominate the midfield. It was not enough to completely fill the void left behind by Anderson. Not yet, at least. He was replaced after the hour.

Gibbs-White kept dropping deep to link play and fizz diagonal balls into the channels instead of being in the heart of it all further up the field. Even he was over-hitting them.

Glasner became the seventh Forest manager in a row to lose his first Premier League match but insists this will be a long process. It took him a while to get the Eagles soaring.

'There is no button to press,' he said. 'It is getting confidence what we are doing. It is a process. Me and my staff can't come in, put our hands on their shoulders and all of a sudden we play like Real Madrid in the 70s.'

All smiles for Trafford

As the final whistle blew, Leeds' defenders took it in turn to embrace James Trafford. The Leeds keeper was grinning from ear to ear. He needed that. Like McAtee, Trafford is someone trying to settle into life away from Manchester City after his summer move and this was the ideal start.

He didn't have the busiest afternoon, he made one strong diving save to push away Igor Jesus's header, but was neat and tidy and commanded his area. 'He has this natural aura of confidence and calmness around him,' said Farke. 'It's just what we want. He played a decisive part.'

His fellow new signing Harry Wilson, a fine bit of business on a free transfer from Fulham, showed flashes of what he will offer in the forward line, getting on to the end of a cross to poke home what looked like the opener only for his goal to be ruled out for offside.

Is Delap the answer?

Glasner confirmed after the game that Forest are after 'two more players, two different positions and we are trying hard to get these deals done'. One of them is expected to be a striker.

Jesus had a good pre-season but showed here that he doesn't quite have the ruthless killer instinct of an elite striker. Chris Wood has shown that but he's 35 in December. He made a difference when he came on but dragged a good chance wide.

Forest are interested in Liam Delap, and tried to sign him last season. He fits the same profile as Wood but is younger. Chelsea want £50m but you expect Forest could get him for nearer £40m.

BY JAMES SHARPE

Sports.title: Lando Norris on the march again as he claims pole for Dutch Grand Prix - as George Russell boosted on return from summer break
Sports.content:
Lando Norris wears No1 on his back and on his car, but it has not seemed that way as often as he would have liked during his title defence.

Yet it is from that position he will start the Dutch Grand Prix, just as he did in Budapest three weeks ago, when he won. All of which are signs that his McLaren team might be on a march after upgrades that are confounding a lack of early-season form.

This time, as spits and spots of rain hit the resort of Zandvoort, a 30-minute rail ride from Amsterdam, the world champion secured his excellent pole one-tenth of a second ahead of compatriot George Russell.

It was, however, a seriously encouraging day for Russell on Formula One’s resumption after the summer break and a number of bumps for him and his lofty expectations of title glory.

He, unlike Norris – who is 90 points off the top of the standings – is still contending towards the front of the world championship reckoning. And his hopes were first rejuvenated earlier in the afternoon when he won the sprint race from pole position in a procession he dominated clinically.

Points in the sprint are meagre, though. So, by finishing ahead of his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who came fourth, Russell only narrowed his deficit to him from 59 points to 56. Big deal, you might say. But it was a major psychological leap when he most needed it.

Lando Norris will start the Dutch Grand Prix on pole with signs McLaren are now on the march

George Russell earned a boost by qualifying ahead of his team-mate Kimi Antonelli

And that was before he qualified a place above Antonelli, the Italian wonderkid who is in serious danger of upsetting what was meant to be Russell’s season of fulfilment.

Clearly relieved post-qualifying, Russell said: ‘The truth is Kimi has been doing an amazing job. We have different driving styles. It is working well for him and these tyres.

‘I’m trying to implement something similar into my driving style. It is like changing your golf swing. You will probably take half a step back first before making improvements.

‘The break allowed me to put my learning to the back of my mind, not fixating on what I want to achieve with the car, but still knowing what I need to do and driving more freely.

‘In tennis, the racquet is basically the same. The lines are always the same distance apart. This isn’t the way it is in Formula One, so I am pleased with how I have managed to adjust to this year’s regulations.

‘I feel very confident going into the race.’

Antonelli registered Russell’s green shoots of revival, however tentative they might be for now. ‘It was a very good wake-up call today,’ admitted the 19-year-old. ‘You can never lower your guard.’

Norris, who had been downbeat after the sprint, in which he finished third, said: ‘A good turnaround from earlier today, where I felt we struggled. Credit to the team, they did a good job.

‘We had to try something because what we had before wasn’t going to be enough. We made some small changes. Enough to give me more confidence. And on a track like Zandvoort you need confidence. You want to attack a lot and I felt I could do that more, so it paid off.

Lewis Hamilton qualified fifth for Ferrari, a place behind Norris’s team-mate Oscar Piastri. He never quite seemed in the frame for pole.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool £140m Barcola issue, Arteta contacts Alvarez, Spurs close to huge deal

Deadline day is creeping closer with just ten days left for Premier League clubs to complete their squads before they're locked in until the turn of the year. Sports.title: Jamie Carragher fires early Man Utd dig as 'carried away' remark comes full cricle
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher fires early Man Utd dig as 'carried away' remark comes full cricle

Jamie Carragher claimed on Friday night that the predictions for Manchester United this season were potentially over the top with the Red Devils then going down to Hull

View Image Jamie Carragher has revelled in Man Utd's opening loss (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher was quick to reference his Manchester United comments after their loss to Hull on Saturday with a witty post on his social media.

‌



Michael Carrick enjoyed an impressive interim spell last season, which saw United rise up to third and secure a Champions League spot. Among his landmark results was a win over Liverpool at Old Trafford.

‌



The Red Devils' renaissance last term, coupled with some of their midfield signings in the form of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, has seen plenty tip United to secure another top four finish. Some have gone as far as to back them to finish second behind Arsenal.

‌



Carragher felt some of the fanfare was over the top and claimed: "People are getting very carried away with Man United. People are putting them second and third, honestly. Man United's back four is the same back four they had five years ago."

The former Liverpool man had his usual back and forth with Sky Sports colleague Gary Neville but, in the aftermath of United's loss at the MKM Stadium to newly promoted Hull, Carragher used a GIF to highlight his comments from Friday night.

‌



Neville had claimed that United were in a better place than Liverpool, but Carragher suggested that Liverpool's starting XI would still be better than their rivals. Both Neville and Carragher will have to give their Premier League predictions on Monday Night Football, which they do annually, but the latter will likely poke fun at Neville over the result.

United were heavy favourites going into Saturday's lunchtime kick-off by were 2-0 down by half-time. They struggled to offer anything in the second-half and returned to Manchester with no points and no goals after a thoroughly underwhelming performance.

‌



Carrick said on their performance: "It was never going to be perfect today but I think going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult, probably a typical one of those games of a newly promoted team at home.

"You can't give them much, they've got a lot to hold on to, and then after that, we had moments, we had opportunities, we just didn't have that spark to then put the chances away or create any more. Listen, we're bitterly disappointed with the result today but it won't knock us.”

Sports.title: Liverpool star told he must tear up his contract to seal return to former club
Sports.content:
Liverpool star told he must tear up his contract to seal return to former club

Celta Vigo want to re-sign Liverpool midfielder Stefan Bajcetic, who has struggled with injuries and has been made available for a permanent transfer by Andoni Iraola

View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic could leave Liverpool (Image: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool midfielder Stefan Bajcetic has been told he needs to terminate his contract in order to secure a move back to former club Celta Vigo.

‌



Bajcetic has struggled massively with injuries over the past few years and is not part of Andoni Iraola's plans this season. The 21-year-old came through the Celta Vigo academy before joining the Reds in 2020 - and he is now wanted back in Spain.

‌



Having previously been linked with Getafe, it is Vigo who are now reportedly leading the race. Bajcetic made an impact under Jurgen Klopp's management but hasn't featured for the first team in over two years, due to injuries and loan spells.

‌



He has spent time away with Red Bull Salzburg and Las Palmas and Liverpool now want to seal a permanent deal. There is a sticking point, however, with Bajcetic being asked to walk away from his Liverpool contract, which doesn't expire until June 2027.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Spanish newspaper Faro de Vigo report that his former club want him to terminate his deal early - like Mohamed Salah did this summer before joining Trabzonspor - and re-join on a free transfer. They would then put him into their under-21s side initially as a way to nurse him back to full fitness.

Liverpool have just waved goodbye to Curtis Jones, who completed a £30million (€35m) transfer to Inter Milan on Friday. But they are still keen to find a new club for Bajcetic who hasn't delivered on his initial promise.

"If he's happy and we can reach an agreement, it would be a good situation, but I'm not thinking about that right now," Celta Vigo head coach Claudio Giráldez said. "He's a homegrown player; I don't talk about players we don't have.

‌



View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic hasn't played for Liverpool in two years (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"If I talk about any of them, it's those who have been here before because we understand that we always have a stronger connection, and on top of that, we have a very good relationship. I coached him. If it happens, great, but I don't talk about players we don't have.”

Offloading unwanted players is part of Liverpool's transfer plan for the remainder of the summer transfer window, which closes on September 1.

‌



"Some deals you have to wait until the end," Iraola explained in an interview with Sky Sports this week. "But the end is the important picture, the one we will have on September 1, because it is true that we are still quite thin."

Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola remains the number one transfer target, but Liverpool have also been chasing Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh. Brighton have rejected a second bid worth £60m for Minteh and want £70m for the former Newcastle player.

Sports.title: Arsenal dealt Kenan Yildiz blow as transfer hopes ended - 'They can offer whatever'
Sports.content:
Arsenal dealt Kenan Yildiz blow as transfer hopes ended - 'They can offer whatever'

Arsenal remain in the market for a new forward but, after missing out on Vinicius Jnr, Juventus have made it clear that they will not sell Kenan Yildiz

View 2 Images Juventus star Kenan Yildiz has continued to impress in Turin (Image: Filippo Alfero - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images)

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti insists Arsenal "can offer whatever they like" but the Italians will not be selling Kenan Yildiz.

‌



The north Londoners failed with an initial enquiry for Yildiz earlier this summer and the Old Lady have now made it clear they're not prepared to entertain the forward's sale.

‌



Juventus are ultimately in no hurry to sell and have the 21-year-old tied down on a contract until 2030, which he signed back in February. Yildiz scored 11 times in 47 outings last term and his displays saw him named the Serie A Rising Star of the Season.

‌



Yildiz has continued to blossom since heading to Juventus as a free agent from the Bayern academy in 2022 and Spalletti is now adamant that, regardless of what figure is produce, the club will not sell their young star.

‌



“His future is already important staying at Juventus, not because there are other clubs who want to spend €100m for him. We are all convinced that we can show the total potential of Kenan, and he is a potential phenomenon of football. The fans are convinced too.”

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold reveals abuse after Liverpool exit but still watches every game
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold reveals abuse after Liverpool exit but still watches every game

Trent Alexander-Arnold speaks exclusively to the Mirror about his acrimonious move to Real Madrid in his first wide-ranging interview

View 3 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold opens up to the Mirror (Image: Daily Mirror)

Trent Alexander-Arnold has laid bare the scale of abuse he received after leaving Liverpool but says he will always love his boyhood club and watches every game.

‌



The England star has opened up in depth for the first time about his acrimonious departure to Real Madrid last year including being booed on his return to Anfield.

‌



He says there was a difference between supporters expressing their fury inside a football stadium and the “stuff that crossed the line”.

‌



He said: “Abuse online and threats made via social DMs or in other ways are a sad part of life in 2026 if you’re in the public eye and doing things that create a lot of attention. I choose to keep those things away from me because they don’t feel real.”

He adds: “I can rationalise that by knowing it’s not representative of a football club I love, LFC, and it’s not representative of my home city.”

The right-back returned to Anfield last November for a Champions League match in which they lost 1-0. Alexander-Arnold was jeered by fans when he was introduced from the bench in the 80th minute, as well as during the warm-up.

‌



He said: “The booing and disappointment from Liverpool supporters is something I’m absolutely able to shoulder. I can understand it, in my own way. I heard a lot during that period that Liverpool fans didn’t want to be told how to feel or think, and I agree. But I hope one day there’ll be a degree of understanding about the decisions I wanted to make around my own life.

“It hurts because of how much I’ve put into the club over the course of 20 years and the sacrifices I made for the club during that period. So of course it hurts, but I understand the disappointment. I even understand anger expressed through booing.”

View 3 Images Trent opens up (Image: Daily Mirror)

‌



As well as anger inside the stadium, the word "rat" was repeatedly daubed over a mural celebrating Alexander-Arnold nearby. The football ace was sent the image by a friend, and it weighed on him when he returned to the city for the match.

“Going back to Liverpool after everything that’s happened it was on my mind,” he says, adding that his family were also left upset.

“If I'm honest, if something affects me and upsets me, it shows in my family as well. They are in it with me…we’re together.”

‌



Alexander-Arnold found the whole day hard to process. He admits: “Even from the outset, even the thought of going into the away changing room was strange. I’d never actually stepped foot in there before.”

The football star believes the wider impact of online abuse is a serious issue, although one he feels ultimately needs to be addressed by politicians and technology companies. Alexander-Arnold, who has also previously suffered abhorrent racist abuse online, said: “On threats to people via social media, social media pile-ons and the impact they can have on people’s mental health, I think that’s a proper topic.

“But it’s for governments and tech companies to solve. I’ve kind of protected myself from that as much as possible, but I get that for some people it’s not possible.”

‌



Alexander-Arnold has found reassurance in the stark difference between the vitriol directed at him online and the reception he receives when he actually returns to Merseyside.

“Since leaving for Real Madrid, I’ve been back to Liverpool to visit family on a number of occasions,” he said.

“I’ve bumped into lots of fellow Scousers and Reds when I’ve been on my travels. Not a single interaction I’ve had in person reflects the sort of stuff you get online or via social media. So that helps me disassociate it.

‌



“This isn’t me saying everyone in Liverpool is fine with me leaving the club. Of course they aren’t. But that’s very different from the stuff that goes beyond the football. It’s why I don’t allow myself to get too down about it and I don’t dwell on it.”

The intensity of the reaction reflected Alexander-Arnold’s unique relationship with Liverpool. A local boy who joined the academy aged six, he rose through the ranks to play 259 times for the club. Yet for all the bitterness surrounding his departure, Alexander-Arnold’s own feelings towards Liverpool appear strikingly unchanged.

“I still watch every game,” he said. “I support them. I want to see them do well. I enjoy watching them, and there will always be a place in my heart for Liverpool, no matter what. It is home to me. It’s the place that gave me the opportunities to go and do what I’ve done and I will always love it. It’s always a place that I’ll call home.”

‌



View 3 Images Trent talks to the Mirror (Image: Daily Mirror)

Alexander-Arnold also spoke of his heartache after missing out on England’s World Cup squad as he remembers the day earlier this year when Thomas Tuchel broke the news to him.

“I was aware the calls were underway,” he said. “Other players I knew had had their call the day before. I’ll be honest, I was full of hope. When the call came, I was at home in Madrid. I had some family over visiting and I went to my bedroom to take the call. When I put the phone down, I was properly gutted. Absolutely gutted. I’d made no plans for my summer because I hoped I’d be in the squad.”

‌



Alexander-Arnold had continued pushing to force his way into Tuchel’s plans and felt his performances during the closing stages of the season had given him reason to believe he might make it.

The rejection left him not merely disappointed but furious too. “I hope the coaching staff would expect and understand that I was angry,” he said. “He wants players who are desperate to play for England. I am one of those. I think he would respect the fact that it really hurt me and prefer that to me not being bothered.”

That hurt is particularly acute given the fierce competition Alexander-Arnold has faced throughout his international career. “We’ve had a lot of really, really good right-backs in this generation that I’ve been playing in so far,” he said. “There’s been a lot of competition, and the managers choose who they feel is the best fit for the team. That’s never really been me so far. But I guess I use it as motivation to push.”

‌



And unlike players who have publicly aired their frustrations after being overlooked, Alexander-Arnold believes there was little to be gained by complaining in the immediate aftermath.

“Some things just don’t need to be said,” he said. “I think everybody would have known that I was disappointed. Speaking out in public is not going to change the manager’s decision. He’s made his mind up. He’s decided what he has. There’s no changing it. Life goes on.”

Alexander-Arnold watched England throughout the World Cup and insists his exclusion has done nothing to diminish his determination to represent his country.

‌



“Until I retire, I’m still an England player, whether I’m selected or not,” he said. “I’m always available if and when the manager needs me. There’s no bigger honour.”

And rather than allowing the rejection to consume him, he plans to use it to drive his attempt to force his way back into Tuchel’s thinking. “I’ll take those feelings into this season and turn them into a positive,” he said. “I want to use it as fuel to get back into England squads and then back in an England shirt. That’s an aim of mine and I hope to achieve it.”

Alexander-Arnold has told how he struggled in the aftermath of Liverpool forward Diogo Jota's death in a car crash, aged 28. The football star was in America at the Club World Cup with his new team Real Madrid when his former teammate was tragically killed.

‌



And he says how being so far away from Liverpool and his ex-colleagues in the US was a “very, very difficult time.”

He said: “I think that's what was difficult….going through it on your own. Everybody else who had known him for that amount of time were all grouped together. It was difficult, and then having to continue to play games and them being so far away was hard. But coming back to Anfield and being able to go to the stadium and put some flowers down really helped me get that closure.”

Opening up about Diogo, he said the two of them “spoke every day.” He added: “I was injured a couple of times when he was and we were doing our training to get back fit together, and we were both very competitive.

Article continues below

“So we would always, you know, have different competitions between ourselves. Those are the kind of memories that I'll hold close to me. He was just a really good guy. Like he was very honest. That's one of the best attributes that anybody can have. He was hardworking. He loved what he did, and was a massive family man. "

Sports.title: Rossa Ryan's piece of advice inspires Sky Bet Ebor win by Alan King-trained Daiquiri Bay
Sports.content:
Rossa Ryan's piece of advice inspires Sky Bet Ebor win by Alan King-trained Daiquiri Bay

The 10-1 chance held on in an exciting finish to the £500,000 feature race on Saturday, crossing the line front of the Wathnan Racing-owned pair Hopewell Rock and Opportunity

View 2 Images Jockey Rossa Ryan after riding Daiquiri Bay to victory in the Sky Bet Ebor (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Rossa Ryan was praised for inspiring the Sky Bet Ebor success by talented stayer Daiquiri Bay on the final day of York's racing festival.

‌



The rider pipped the Wathnan Racing-owned pair Hopewell Rock and Opportunity by a head and a neck aboard the 10-1 chance, trained Alan King.

‌



Ryan rode Daiquiri Bay to win the Copper Horse Stakes at Royal Ascot earlier in the season, when the chestnut gelding lowered the track record.

‌



Not seen on a racecourse for two months, a 67-day break was no problem for the upwardly mobile handicapper, who travelled nicely through the field and found enough to hold on in a close finish.

"Full marks to Rossa, we sat down after Ascot and he said put him away and freshen him up," said King, delighted to go two places better than Salsalino's third when favourite in 2003.

Jockey Juan Hernandez rushes to Nunthorpe victory then dashes by helicopter to Heathrow READ MORE :

Race meeting abandoned after two jockeys sent to hospital following heavy falls READ MORE :

"He had a hard race and broke the track record. We haven't missed a beat in the last three weeks. He's a tough horse and it was a great ride. I'm blown away."

‌



Ryan, disappointed to be pipped in the Yorkshire Oaks on the unlucky-in-running Sparan Nua on Wednesday, also had to settle for second in yesterday's Nunthorpe partnering Starlust, who was no match for US raider Bacio.

But while he was out of luck in the Grade One contests, it changed in the highly valuable handicap which rounds off the four-day racing week on the Knavesmire.

View 2 Images The top three dash for the line (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And Ryan was only freed up to compete at the prestigious meeting after a 28-day race-riding ban was reduced to ten on appeal, the original punishment handed out for easing Thunder Home prematurely at Sandown on July 23.

The panel did not accept that the young thoroughbred would inevitably have won had the rider pushed out continuously.

"The man's a genius," said Ryan about King, who has collected numerous top prizes on the Flat and over jumps.

Article continues below

"We’ve had a year where, luckily, we’ve been able to plan him out. After Ascot I thought I'd leave Daiquiri Bay and come straight here. Alan agreed and he had him spot on."

Ebor gambles on Willie Mullins' number one Love Me Tender (7-2 favourite) and another Irish raider Emit (4-1) from Joseph O'Brien's stable, went astray.

Ascending (28-1) filled fourth as the field of 22 horses passed the post, with Beylerbeyi (20-1) in fifth for the boosted each-way places with some bookmakers.

Medical teams from both sides rushed onto the pitch to assist Castro, with A Bola explaining that a defibrillator was used. Unfortunately, attempts to resuscitate the Portuguese talent were unsuccessful.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
