Sports.title: Why Honda's new F1 engine comes with fresh but expected driveability issues
Sports.content:
Aston Martin Formula 1 driver Fernando Alonso says more work is needed to optimise Honda's more powerful engine after struggling to keep his car on the track in sprint qualifying at Zandvoort.

Alonso and team-mate Lance Stroll have received the second specification of Honda's V6 power unit, with the Japanese manufacturer having earmarked the Netherlands as the site to deploy its one in-season engine upgrade this year.

The engine was shaken down during a filming day after the Hungarian Grand Prix at the end of July, but while running the new unit in anger both drivers encountered fresh driveability issues on Friday in Zandvoort.

Alonso went off in Turn 1 during SQ1, complaining of heavy vibrations from the engine before qualifying 22nd and last, three seconds off the pace. Stroll fared little better, getting ahead of both Cadillac cars but still ending the day a distant 19th.

"Free practice was more or less okay but in qualifying we had problems on the engine," Alonso reported. "Driveability was pushing on the braking, so it was difficult to stop the car sometimes because the engine was over-delivering.

"And then apparently the SLM mode [the lower drag setting on the 2026 car] didn't work for me so I could not open the rear wing. A combination of both made the laps very tricky.

"When you brake and the throttle is open, it's difficult to stop the car."

Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

Stroll similarly grappled with the behaviour of his new power unit: "We were struggling with the driveability, and there were a few other things that weren’t quite right, so we need to understand why.

"It’s really windy out there, but it’s the same for everyone. We’ll go through everything tonight, look at the data, and try to make some improvements for tomorrow.”

Honda's homework starts over

On the surface Friday's performance feels like a puzzling step backwards for Aston Martin and Honda after its huge Hungary car upgrade moved the Silverstone squad back into the heart of F1's midfield.

But Honda had already calculated that bringing the new power unit would mean that a lot of the work the Japanese brand did at the start of the season to improve its subpar driveability would have to be largely re-done for the latest specification.

"We developed our tools to optimise our driveability. We have made good progress, and we were close to what we wanted to achieve," Honda's F1 project leader Shintaro Orihara told Autosport in a wide-ranging interview.

"But when we introduce the spec 2 engine, the combustion characteristics will change. There will be a big difference.

"And then engine behaviour will be changed in the cornering phase as well, so we need to develop our driveability again."

Sports.title: The advice Marquez gave Hadjar over his wrist injury
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar misses this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix after sustaining a wrist injury during a gym session last week. According to Racing Bulls CEO Peter Bayer, Red Bull’s sister team was informed on Friday of a potential driver change, with the situation developing further on Tuesday.

That was when Yuki Tsunoda was called up – having been on a beach in Greece when he was asked to step in – while Liam Lawson was handed another opportunity at Red Bull following his demotion after the 2025 Chinese Grand Prix.

Read Also: Formula 1 The full circle moment given to Lawson at the 2026 Dutch GP

While the situation naturally presents opportunities for both drivers, it is highly frustrating for Hadjar, who nevertheless made an appearance in the Zandvoort paddock on Friday morning.

Hadjar claimed his maiden F1 podium in the Netherlands last year and had planned to reference that achievement with a playful nod in a special helmet design this year.

Red Bull and Marquez in agreement: Take your time to recover

Hadjar – as you might expect from any athlete – wanted to go racing again straight away, but he has been advised by two different parties not to take any risks and to sit out the Dutch GP.

First of all, that message came from Red Bull. Laurent Mekies confirmed that his team did not want to take any risks with Max Verstappen's team-mate, who has performed surprisingly well this year.

Hadjar had planned a special helmet design for this weekend, inspired by Delft blue pottery and his broken trophy from last year Photo by: Red Bull Content Pool

"Isack is alright," Mekies told the official F1 website. "We have no reason to take any risk with him. He has done a fantastic start of the season, he has been stronger and stronger every time he has been driving this car out of the garage, session after session, weekend after weekend.

"We take zero risk, we let him sort out the recovery this weekend, and hopefully we’ll have him very, very quickly [back] in the car."

The advice to skip Zandvoort also came from another, more surprising source: seven-time MotoGP world champion Marc Marquez.

The Ducati rider and Hadjar share the same physiotherapist, Carlos J. Garcia. Hadjar called Marquez after sustaining the wrist injury, with the Spaniard advising him not to rush his return.

The rider currently fourth in the MotoGP standings also urged Hadjar not to rush into certain medical procedures, given that the Frenchman is still young and has a long F1 career ahead of him.

Marquez therefore felt that taking his time and recovering properly was the most sensible approach for Hadjar, which is exactly what Red Bull had already told the youngster.

Marquez himself has plenty of first-hand experience when it comes to injuries. The MotoGP icon has, among other things, broken his right upper arm and right thumb, dislocated both shoulders and suffered from diplopia.

Marquez is known for returning quickly after injury, but advised Hadjar to do the opposite Photo by: Qian Jun / MB Media via Getty Images

When can Hadjar return for Red Bull?

The key question, of course, is when Hadjar will be able to return behind the wheel of the RB22.

When asked by Autosport, Red Bull said it is still too early to provide an official update on that, although the plan is to have him back in the car at Monza for the Italian GP in two weeks' time.

"It's too early to say that definitely, but it’s our target to have him back in Monza," Mekies told Sky Sports Germany.

The Italian GP will take place on the weekend of 4-6 September. Although the iconic circuit in Monza's park is certainly not the most physically demanding track on the calendar, the Spanish GP at the new Madring follows just one week later.

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Russell takes pole in tight sprint qualifying with Antonelli fifth
Sports.content:
George Russell has taken pole position for the Dutch Grand Prix sprint race with Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli down in fifth.

The Mercedes driver pipped reigning world champion Lando Norris by only 0.041s to take his third sprint pole of the 2026 season.

Russell’s pole came particularly out of the blue after topping neither SQ1 or SQ2 - respectively done by Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri - but a 1m11.567s in the final session was enough.

It was a very tight final session too, as third-placed Leclerc was just 0.055s off the pace for Ferrari with Norris’ McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri in fourth and 0.099s behind Russell.

A slightly bigger gap then emerged to Russell’s team-mate Antonelli though, who was 0.227s behind the Briton and suffering floor damage from an off at the penultimate corner in SQ1.

Precisely three tenths behind Antonelli was Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in sixth, one spot ahead of seventh-placed Lewis Hamilton who struggled in the sister Ferrari with a 0.624s gap to Russell.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Alpine’s Pierre Gasly, Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto and Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad respectively rounded out the top 10 at Zandvoort ahead of Saturday’s shortened race.

It was a respectable Red Bull return for Liam Lawson, who has replaced the injured Isack Hadjar, as he qualified 11th after being eliminated by his usual team-mate Lindblad.

“I have no idea what happened,” reported the New Zealander, who was four tenths off SQ3, and will share the sixth row with his Racing Bulls stand-in and F1 returnee Yuki Tsunoda.

Franco Colapinto will be on the seventh row in 13th, shared with 14th-placed Nico Hulkenberg, while Esteban Ocon and Alex Albon respectively rounded out the SQ2 drop zone.

In SQ1 a late improvement from Oliver Bearman put him 17th and one spot above Williams man Carlos Sainz, who was pushed into the elimination zone by Bearman’s Haas team-mate Ocon.

The last four spots were occupied by the usual suspects: Aston Martin’s Lance Stroll in 19th, Cadillac duo Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez 20th and 21st and Fernando Alonso in 22nd.

Alonso particularly struggled as he locked up at Turn 1 and finished last despite a tow from a Cadillac and it was later confirmed that the Straight Line Mode on his rear wing didn’t work.

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Antonelli pips Norris in practice amid poor showing for Red Bull
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli was fastest in practice for the Dutch Grand Prix as the championship leader picked up where he left off upon Formula 1’s return from its summer break.

The Mercedes star set a 1m12.949s lap at Zandvoort and was the only driver to go sub-1m13s as second-place went to McLaren’s reigning world champion Lando Norris with a 1m13.070s.

Drivers were quick to head out for the sole practice session of this sprint weekend - one where Zandvoort bids farewell to F1 - with intermediates the initial choice on a damp seaside track.

But conditions were drying, Nico Hulkenberg saying “I think it’s slicks” almost instantly, so it didn’t take long to ditch the intermediates with Oscar Piastri using mediums five minutes in.

The McLaren driver set the pace on a 1m23.311s, 2.251s quicker than Lewis Hamilton who was fastest on intermediates, before reducing that to a 1m20.480s with his next lap.

That drastic improvement was a sign of things to come on the evolving surface as Antonelli surged to the top with a 1m18.264s, 1m16.112s and then a 1m15.531s on his opening three tours.

So the lap times kept tumbling, Hamilton, George Russell and Charles Leclerc all greeted the top of the leaderboard, while Antonelli also endured a 360-degree spin at Turn 10 halfway through the one-hour session. “I don’t know what the heck happened there,” reported the Mercedes driver.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Everything naturally ramped up when the soft tyre runs commenced with 10 minutes remaining and Piastri was first to beat Leclerc’s medium benchmark (1m14.146s) by setting a 1m13.608s.

Piastri wasn’t fastest for long though as Leclerc regained top spot by 0.261s, before a 1m13.139s lap for Ferrari team-mate Hamilton put him 0.208s quicker.

But there was yet more change in the final five minutes on a busy circuit as Norris went quickest with a 1m13.105s, subsequently beaten by Antonelli who was 0.156s faster.

That was enough for the championship leader, who holds a 50-point advantage over runner-up Hamilton, to remain top as Norris failed to improve on his final lap.

There was a late change for third though, as Antonelli’s team-mate George Russell - who is 59 points behind the Italian - set a 1m13.074s to go 0.065s quicker than fourth-placed Hamilton.

Leclerc rounded out the top five with a lap that was 0.289s off the pace and it was a big gap to Piastri in sixth as the Australian’s 1m13.608s put him 0.659s behind Antonelli.

So the top three teams - Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren - occupied the first six spots as usual, whereas seventh went to Audi’s Hulkenberg who impressively set a 1m13.784s with the mediums late on.

Yuki Tsunoda, Racing Bulls Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

Team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto opted for a similar strategy with a 1m13.992s late on and he finished ninth, with Alpine’s Pierre Gasly splitting the pair after setting a 1m13.911s on hards.

Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad (1m14.285s) completed the top 10 in a poor session for Red Bull, who respectively finished 11th and 14th via Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar’s stand-in Liam Lawson.

The four-time world champion, who on Thursday announced his contract renewal, reported problems with downshifts and oversteer and had an off heading into the final corner.

Sprint qualifying is up next on Friday afternoon.

Sports.title: Small change made “unbelievable” improvement in Hamilton’s Ferrari | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton is optimistic about his chances in the Dutch Grand Prix after making a significant improvement in his Ferrari’s balance in qualifying.

He said he was surprised how much better his car felt on his way to fifth on the grid in qualifying after finishing seventh in the sprint race earlier today.

“I’m so much happier with the car,” said Hamilton. “Honestly, it’s crazy. We changed a lot of things, it doesn’t really look that big, but the difference it makes in the car is unbelievable.”

Hamilton said he felt happy with the car at the beginning of the weekend before qualifying for the sprint race.

“The difficult thing is I started P1 with good confidence, I lost it all in [sprint race] qualifying and all through the race I had no confidence in the balance. It was constantly breaking away from me.

“Then I go into [grand prix] qualifying and the car’s there, so the balance is there at least. So I was building and building and building. [If we had] some more laps I think we could have probably done better but I think ultimately the tyres were the issue for us.”

The Ferrari driver said he feels “a lot more optimistic for tomorrow with the balance that I have.”

However his team mate Charles Leclerc, who finished second in the sprint race, was less happy after taking sixth on the grid for the grand prix.

“We’ll have to look at two things, really,” he said. “The first one is mostly the fact that we started changing engine modes from Q1 to Q2 to Q3. Then the car is just doing different things underneath me, which is not something I enjoy, and we’ve probably missed a bit of performance there.

“Second is the prep[aration] lap that we have done that the others seem to not have done. I don’t feel like my tyres would have been ready without that preparation lap, but we’ve got to be open-minded and look at what the others have done.”

Sports.title: Lawson pleased with “good lap” after qualifying a tenth off Verstappen on return | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Liam Lawson said he was pleased with his performance after qualifying one tenth of a second off team mate Max Verstappen on his return to Red Bull.

Red Bull dropped Lawson after his first two appearances for the team last year. On his final appearance, in Shanghai, Lawson qualified 0.75 seconds slower than the four-times world champion.

The two Red Bull drivers will share the fourth row of the grid for Sunday’s grand prix. “It was good, it was an improvement from yesterday in just putting everything together,” said Lawson, who qualified 11th for the sprint race the day before.

“To get to that point in quali is good,” he continued. “Overall we wanted probably more from the car, but obviously my only reference at the moment is Max and I’ve just been trying to get closer through the weekend. I feel like honestly I did a good lap so overall I’m happy with that side of it.”

Lawson, who has been driving for Racing Bulls so far this year and lied ninth in the championship, said his goal for the grand prix is to at least hold on to eighth place.

“At least staying where we are, that would be really, really good, but trying to move forward as well if the opportunity is there,” he said. “Obviously, I’m still learning this car in the race. Today was quite tricky, but I have a bit of data to review to try and help that.”

Verstappen said he did not think he could have got much more out of his car. “There was not a lot more in it, to be honest,” he said. “I didn’t feel like I left anything on the table, which is not where I wanted to be.”

This is the first time Verstappen has qualified lower than third on the grid for his home race. He said he had “the same balance limitations as I had yesterday” despite making changes to his set-up after the sprint race.

“I think there’s some fundamental things in the car hopefully we can fix for next year,” he said. “The rest is maybe trying to find a bit more performance, but we’ll see of course in the coming races.”

Sports.title: Norris beats Mercedes pair to Dutch Grand Prix pole position | 2026 Dutch Grand Prix qualifying report
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed pole position for the second grand prix in a row, denying the Mercedes drivers in a closely-fought session.

The front-running drivers hurried to complete their final runs as rain threatened to fall during the deciding moments of Q3. Norris, who held provisional pole position ahead of George Russell following the first runs, raced to keep his rival behind him after they joined the track for their final runs.

Both followed Andrea Kimi Antonelli in the other Mercedes who went fastest with his final run. Norris beat his time by more than a tenth of a second, however, then Russell split the pair of them. Oscar Piastri ensured Mercedes-powered cars filled the top four places.

The Ferrari drivers gambled with the weather and completed their final runs after their rivals. Lewis Hamilton beat his team mate’s time and the pair will share the third row of the grid. The Red Bull duo claimed the fourth row, Liam Lawson impressively lapping just a tenth of a second slower than Max Verstappen on his return to the team.

Yuki Tsunoda could not join his team mate Arvid Lindblad in Q3 on his return to Formula 1. Lindblad took 10th on the grid behind Gabriel Bortoleto, who scraped through the first round after a slow first run and a significant snap of oversteer at the exit of Tarzan.

Neither Alpine driver made the cut for Q3, including Pierre Gasly who had the benefit of the team’s upgrade. He fell short by a tenth of a second. Nico Hulkenberg also dropped out in Q2.

Alexander Albon was the only Williams driver to reach Q2, beating team mate Carlos Sainz Jnr by a few hundredths of a second. Both of the upgraded Aston Martins went out in the first round, ahead of Oliver Bearman and the two Cadillacs.

Sports.title: McLaren’s car is “terrible” in low-speed corners – Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
McLaren’s performance in Zandvoort highlights their car’s weakness in slow corners, says Lando Norris.

The reigning world champion won the previous round at the Hungaroring, a circuit which has several low-to-medium-speed corners, but he believes the slower mix of corners at Zandvoort is a problem for the MCL40.

“We knew in Budapest we’re very good in high-speed corners and we’re pretty terrible in slow speed, but we still managed to win,” he said. “Here there’s a lot more of the very, very slow speed and more of our problems show. So [it’s] not a surprise at all. It’s exactly what we expected.”

McLaren have brought further upgrades for their car in Zandvoort. Norris said these have performed as expected but the team still has a significant deficit to its rivals at some circuits.

“They’ve done exactly as they should, so I’m very happy,” he said. “We still managed to progress.

“It’s just [in] certain areas we’re just nowhere near quick enough. The slow speed, we’ve just struggled the whole weekend and seems clearly the weakness we have in the car at the minute. I feel if we still went back to Monaco now, we’re going to be shocking, as we were.

“So I think we’ve clearly progressed a lot, and especially in medium and high-speed, which is why we’re quick here, why we were so quick in Budapest. It wasn’t like we were quick everywhere in Budapest, and that’s why we won. The slow speed, we were still slower than Ferrari and matching Mercedes just about.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“So we still have weaknesses, even though we managed to win one race. It’s just the strengths really shone there, and here it’s just the deficit is too big in the slow speed.”

Norris qualified second on the grid for today’s sprint race alongside George Russell but fell to third behind Charles Leclerc. He doubts McLaren can make any significant changes to the car’s poor performance in low-speed corners for the time being.

“There’s just nothing we can do about it now. It’s just how the car is for the time being.

“That’s where we still have to focus as a team. We’ll try and get everything out of it. I feel like I still did a good job today, even with the P3.

“It’s just [that] I want to be fighting for top spot and be fighting and going forward and catching George and putting him under pressure rather than trying to survive in every slow-speed corner and fighting for my life.

“So I’m very happy with the team and the progress we made, and the upgrades have all worked, and they’ve allowed me to be P3 today. But we just need more if we want to fight for a championship.”

Sports.title: ‘A sprint race at Zandvoort is not going to be the most exciting’ – Lindblad | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Arvid Lindblad was not surprised the Dutch Grand prix sprint race lacked action.

Only a single position change occured in the top half of the field after the first lap. Lindblad spent his entire race behind Gabriel Bortoleto

“I think we all knew a sprint race at Zandvoort’s probably not going to be the most exciting race,” said Lindblad.

This weekend’s sprint race is the fifth of the six Formula 1 will hold this year. It is the first time Zandvoort has held a sprint race, though the track does not have a contract to hold another grand prix in the future.

Despite the lack of action in his race, Lindblad said the session was useful for practice. “It’s another 20, 25 laps under my belt on a new track for me which is going to very useful for the rest of the weekend,” he said.

“I think the pace is honestly better than expected. We normally struggle a little bit more in the race than quali and considering we already weren’t great in quali, to be quite competitive, quite easily able to hang on to the two guys in front I think was decent.

“So let’s see for the rest of the weekend, but we know we can make a step forward. I know there’s more to come from me.”

Max Verstappen was another driver who spent his enter race unable to challenge the driver ahead of him. “I just got a bit stuck behind Oscar [Piastri],” he said. “Around here, as soon as you get close your tyres overheat and you can’t pass, so you’re just stuck.”

Sports.title: Diego Pacheco’s November Return Tests Hearn’s Canelo Plan
Sports.content:
EverythingBoxing reported that Pacheco will lead the card, although his opponent, date and venue remain unannounced. Hearn previously named Bruno Surace and Armando Resendiz as possible opponents after Pacheco’s 11th-round stoppage of Immanuwel Aleem in July.

Resendiz is coming off a loss to Munguia. Surace lost his rematch with the Mexican champion, but he also knocked him out in their first fight. Surace’s history makes him dangerous, although beating him may not convince Munguia to face Pacheco.

Getting there will be difficult. Munguia and his promoter must first want the Pacheco fight. Another clinch-heavy performance like the one Pacheco produced against Kevin Lele Sadjo gives them little incentive. Pacheco does not bring the audience or money needed to make an awkward voluntary defense worthwhile.

If Munguia declines, Pacheco would have to become the WBA mandatory and wait for the sanctioning body to order the fight. Mandatory status still would not produce a firm timetable. It would be up to the WBA to force the issue, and as we’ve seen lately, they can be lax about doing that. In other words, Pacheco could become mandatory to Munguia’s belt, and still not get a title shot soon.

The Canelo portion requires even more help. Canelo must defeat WBC champion Christian Mbilli on October 31 to regain the belt and remain active long enough for Hearn’s dream vision to work. Mbilli’s youth, size, pressure and high output present a serious threat to the 36-year-old challenger. Canelo may lose and possibly get knocked out.

Even if Canelo wins, Pacheco offers little in terms of financial value, and has a clinch-heavy style unlikely to create interest on his part.

A more direct option would be IBF champion Osleys Iglesias. Pacheco is ranked No. 13 by the IBF, leaving Hearn room to try to get him a voluntary title shot. Pursuing Iglesias would show Hearn’s confidence in Diego. He would have to believe that he could beat Osleys for him to go that route. Given the way Pacheco looked against Kevin Sadjo, getting hurt repeatedly, it’s unlikely Hearn would take the chance of putting him in with the Cuban Osleys.

The Munguia route is safer than facing Iglesias. It also depends on too many things going Hearn’s way.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Could Fight At MSG Without Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
“I’ve spoken to Spencer Brown today as well, and he’s saying that even if Anthony Joshua doesn’t fight Tyson Fury, that they’ll go ahead and they’ll have a fight for Tyson Fury in America on that day at Madison Square Garden. They will go ahead, and he will have a fight,” said Gareth to iFL TV.

That changes the position of Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn. Refusing the New York deal will not necessarily bring the contest back to Britain next year. Fury could face somebody else while Joshua loses a payday that has been discussed for years.

The contract must be completed early next week, in Davies’ view, because the organizers need enough time to promote the event. He identified Monday through Wednesday as the critical period, although he made clear that this was his reading of the situation rather than an official deadline.

Fury sounded increasingly frustrated on Friday, accusing Joshua and Hearn of holding up the agreement because they want more money.

“It doesn’t look like they’re going to sign the fight, all because Eddie Hearn and [Joshua] want more money. They’ve already had that much money off of Turki [Alalshikh] in the last few years, Eddie and AJ. They’ve had boxing deals, they’ve had darts deals, they’ve had snooker deals. They’ve had everything. “And yet they’ve got the audacity and cheek of flea-bitten rats to ask for more money from Old Turki. That’s hideous. I’ll tell you what, it’s disgusting. Money-thirsty pieces of s***.”

Joshua has already signed for the fight under terms tied to a British venue. Staging it at Madison Square Garden brings different tax and financial considerations, and Hearn wants his fighter to receive the same net purse he would have collected in Britain.

Hearn’s reluctance to accept the relocation may have another explanation. Davies suspects the promoter wants Joshua to take one more fight before risking him against Fury.

The British journalist described Joshua as dangerous during the early rounds but questioned his punch resistance. In his view, a decisive loss to Fury could end Joshua’s career, giving Hearn an incentive to secure another appearance first.

That theory remains speculation. Brown’s statement is the more important development. Fury’s side is prepared to move forward at Madison Square Garden, leaving Joshua with less control over the date than previously thought.

Sports.title: WBA Welterweight Title Clash Rolly Romero  vs Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Throughout his pro career, Rolly Romero was categorized as a hard-hitting puncher who possessed limited boxing skills. He was in the process of building a solid career, but in May 2025, Romero earned a signature win.

As the challenger, Rolly Romero had a big moment when he knocked down Ryan Garcia in the second round. Romero displayed poise and ring generalship as he outpointed Garcia and won the WBA welterweight title.

When it comes to a signature win, Rolly Romero’s upcoming opponent is very familiar with that term. Teofimo Lopez is a boxer who has not one but two certified signature wins.

Back in October 2020, Lopez executed his game plan to perfection as he outboxed a prime Vasiliy Lomachenko. Three years later, Lopez put on another masterclass as he dominated Josh Taylor and won the Ring and the WBO 140-pound world titles.

Lopez would go on to have three successful title defenses. The night of January 31, 2026, was a rough night for Lopez due to the fact that Shakur Stevenson was able to control distance, dictate the pace of the bout, and, as a result, he cruised to a unanimous decision victory.

Now the former two-division world champion Teofimo Lopez will attempt to bounce back in a big way. Lopez will step in the ring and attempt to defeat his close friend and become a three-division world champion.

Teofimo is a boxer-puncher who is explosive, athletic, and a dangerous counterpuncher. Rolly is awkward, but he’s an aggressive fighter who is accustomed to pressing forward and landing power shots from unexpected angles.

When it comes to pure boxing, Teofimo has the advantage. When it comes down to punching power, you have to give the advantage to Rolly.

To win this fight, Teofimo Lopez has to utilize his advantage, which is his skill set. He has to use his jab, control distance, be defensively responsible, and outbox the heavy-handed Romero.

Rolly Romero has to show the poise and discipline he displayed in the fight against Ryan Garcia. He has to set up his shots, because one of his power shots can change the complexion of the fight.

On the night of August 22nd, the question is, will Teofimo Lopez add to his legacy by becoming a three-division world champion, or will Rolly Romero enhance his resume by taking down his second boxing star in a row?

Sports.title: Amanda Serrano Takes KO Chase Into Final Fight
Sports.content:
That gives Serrano’s last appearance a specific target beyond another championship defense.

She remains tied with Christy Martin on 32 professional knockouts and made clear afterward that breaking that mark still appeals to her.

“We still got that 33rd knockout. I got one more fight. If I don’t get it, I’m glad that I tied with Christy Martin.”

Manzur showed why Serrano cannot simply chase the finish.

The 27-year-old contender pushed forward, closed the distance and forced Serrano to work under pressure. Her best spell came in the fourth, when she attacked with Serrano against the ropes and refused to give the champion an easy route back toward center ring.

Serrano relied on body shots and counters to slow that pressure. She found cleaner punches as the fight developed, but Manzur’s willingness to keep coming prevented Serrano from turning those openings into a stoppage.

The scorecards reflected the resistance. One judge scored the fight 114-114, while the other two gave Serrano 116-112 margins.

Afterward, Serrano gave Manzur credit rather than dressing up a difficult night’s work.

“I knew she was tough. She’s young. She’s 27. She’s 10 years younger than me. These girls are getting younger, stronger. Thank God I’m almost out of the game.”

Serrano has already declared that only one fight remains, and at 37 she understands the physical equation has changed while younger challengers continue coming through.

Her 50th professional victory supplied another landmark, although Serrano kept her assessment short.

“I got the 50th win. That’s a milestone on its own.”

Serrano’s final fight should start with the jab, body work and clean counters rather than a reckless hunt for knockout No. 33. Manzur showed that forcing the finish can take Serrano away from the distance and punch selection that create her best openings.

Sports.title: Amanda Serrano vs. Lucrecia Manzur Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Dropped by Mayelli Flores Rosquero in round two, Melissa Mortensen recovered to capture the vacant WBA super bantamweight title through a split decision. Flores continued advancing after the knockdown, but Mortensen raised her output and caught her with the cleaner counters.

All three judges scored the fight 95-94. Two favored Mortensen, giving the Danish fighter her tenth win and first major title, while the remaining card went to Flores.

The fifth round transformed Avious Griffin’s welterweight bout with Jackson Marinez from a cautious contest into a one-sided beating. Griffin closed the distance and registered the first knockdown with two left hooks followed by a right hand. An overhand right and a left hook to the body put Marinez down again later in the round, leading his corner to stop the fight before the sixth began. Nineteen of Griffin’s 20 victories have come by knockout.

Cruiserweight Keno Marley controlled the distance against Braylan Brooks before ending matters with a right hand at 1:46 of round three. Marley used his height and footwork during the opening two rounds, then increased the pressure once Brooks began struggling with the pace.

Another third-round finish followed in the heavyweight division. Nelvie Tiafack overwhelmed Salvador Zavala Molina and handed him his first defeat, although the referee intervened before Molina looked completely unable to continue. Tiafack moved to five professional wins with four stoppages.

An upset arrived at minimumweight when Brook Sibrian defeated Guadalupe Medina by unanimous decision. Repeated attacks to the body allowed Sibrian to force the pace and prevent Medina from controlling the exchanges. The defeat was the first of Medina’s career.

Only 81 seconds were required for Albina Moldazhanova to produce the fastest ending of the event. The southpaw knocked out Sheila Fabiana Liesegang during the opening round of their light welterweight contest, leaving her with five stoppages from five professional appearances.

Four decisions completed the remaining undercard. Cinderella Linnear edged Jully De Oliveira by split decision, with Iyana Verduzco receiving the same verdict against Miguelina Hernandez. At minimumweight, Jocelyn Camarillo outpointed Ashley Felix, while lightweight Paolo Barredo controlled Jorge Garcia across six rounds to secure a unanimous win.

Sports.title: Jahmal Harvey Crushes Keb With Second-Round Knockout
Sports.content:
The punishment continued in the second round. Harvey hurt Keb with a fast combination before landing a crushing right cross that sent him heavily to the canvas and ended the scheduled six-round contest.

The punch statistics showed how one-sided the fight had been. Harvey landed 46 of 84 power punches for a 55 percent connect rate, including 37 shots to the head. Keb connected with only 10 of 44 power punches and landed seven to the head.

Those numbers also raise the question of how quickly MVP will advance Harvey. The 23-year-old was a 2021 amateur world champion and reached the quarterfinals at the Paris Olympics, giving him far more experience than his four professional fights suggest.

Another opponent at Keb’s level will not reveal much. Harvey needs someone capable of surviving his early speed, forcing him to adjust, and making him work through difficult rounds. His amateur background and rapid start leave little reason to move him at the pace of an ordinary prospect.

The knockout was the strongest performance of Harvey’s young professional career, but the ease of the win made the matchmaking look too safe. His next opponent should offer enough resistance to show how close Harvey is to facing established lightweights.

The bout served as the co-feature of the Amanda Serrano versus Lucrecia Manzur card and streamed free on TikTok LIVE.

Sports.title: Bradley Questions Ryan Garcia But Gives Benn A Pass
Sports.content:
“You want to be a fighter or you want to be a social media darling? Pick one. Boxing gets jealous. Your mitt work, I’m looking at it like, ‘Where is the intensity?’ There ain’t no intensity in that. Have a real camp. I hope this is just for the people and you’re not really showing what you’re doing,” Bradley said on his channel.

A short training clip does not reveal everything Garcia is doing. Bradley also fails to give Ryan credit for redeeming himself against Mario Barrios in his last fight. Garcia arrived in good condition, remained composed and showed that the Rolando Romero loss had not destroyed him.

Rolly presented a different physical threat. He looked enormous inside the ring and repeatedly threw double left hooks that rattled Garcia. Ryan seemed to underestimate Romero’s size and power, then failed to adjust once those hooks began landing.

Against Regis Prograis, Benn struggled throughout, taking shots and unable to hurt him. He came down to 150 pounds for their April catchweight fight and absorbed plenty of punishment despite winning a 10-round unanimous decision.

Making the 147-pound welterweight limit requires Benn to drop three additional pounds. That cut may reduce his strength, punch resistance and ability to maintain pressure.

Pressure remains Benn’s best method of testing Garcia by attacking early and denying him room, but rushing forward carries danger. Ryan owns the faster hands and the left hook smash that he’s known for. Romero’s double left hook troubled him because it was delivered by a much larger man with unusual power. Benn may not carry the same force at 147.

By studying Ryan’s social media clips, Bradley is giving Benn the benefit of the doubt. Their recent performances provide a different picture: Garcia responded well against Barrios, while Benn endured a punishing night at a weight three pounds above the one he must reach in Las Vegas.

Ghana News.title: Was Afenyo-Markin’s GoldBod criticism justified or exaggerated?
Ghana News.content:
There is a serious national conversation to be had about GoldBod, the Bank of Ghana, the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, public finances and the environmental consequences of gold mining. Unfortunately, Alexander Afenyo-Markin appears determined to turn that conversation into a political courtroom in which the verdict is delivered before the evidence is examined.

The first problem is the claim that GoldBod itself made a US$1.7 billion loss in 2025. The IMF material cited in this controversy discusses losses associated with the Bank of Ghana's Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. Indeed, the IMF has separately warned that losses from the DGPP and GoldBod's activities should not be borne by the central bank.

That distinction matters.

Afenyo-Markin is entitled to question government. He is entitled to demand accountability. He is entitled to scrutinise GoldBod's finances. But he is not entitled to make the IMF say what the IMF did not say.

If the claim is that GoldBod made the entire US$1.7 billion loss, then the challenge is embarrassingly simple: show us the exact page, paragraph and sentence where the IMF says that.

The IMF's discussion identifies several components of the reported financial outcome, including fees paid to GoldBod, discounts and exchange-rate effects. That is not the same as saying GoldBod itself incurred or caused the entire loss. And GoldBod has presented audited 2025 accounts showing an operational surplus of GH¢907 million and an overall surplus exceeding GH¢5.4 billion.

One can disagree with GoldBod's accounting. One can demand further audits. One can question whether all programme-related risks are captured in its standalone accounts. In fact, Afenyo-Markin has made precisely that argument.

But disagreement is not evidence.

What is even more troubling is the apparent transformation of an accounting debate into a threat of political retribution. Afenyo-Markin has spoken of a future “day of reckoning” for GoldBod officials.

Really?

Since when did an alleged institutional loss automatically become a criminal offence?

A state institution can make an accounting loss without its CEO being a criminal. A valuation loss is not automatically stealing. An exchange-rate loss is not automatically corruption. A policy cost is not automatically financial crime. Before anybody talks about arrest, prosecution and punitive or onerous bail conditions, they should identify the specific offence, the statutory elements and the evidence connecting the individual to the offence.

And frankly, one cannot escape the impression that this has become unusually personal. The repeated focus on Sammy Gyamfi raises a legitimate question: Is this really about GoldBod, or is Sammy Gyamfi himself the target?

If there is evidence of wrongdoing, produce it. If there is a crime, identify it. If there is a loss caused by misconduct, demonstrate the causal connection.

But please, spare Ghanaians the theatre of treating every large number in an IMF report as a criminal indictment.

Ghanaians are discerning. They can read. They can interrogate documents. They can distinguish Bank of Ghana losses from GoldBod's standalone accounts, accounting effects from criminal conduct, and political propaganda from evidence.

Afenyo-Markin may speak with the gravitas of a man delivering the final judgment of the Supreme Court. But a serious voice does not make an unproven claim serious evidence. There are quite a number of allegations he has made that turned out to be inaccurate, to the extent that he was exposed on live television after fact-checkers established that one of his claims was untrue. It is therefore wise for him to hasten slowly and exercise greater caution in making such assertions. Such conduct is unbecoming of a person occupying the office of Minority Leader.

It is therefore fair to compare his performance with that of prominent Minority Leaders who occupied the position before him and distinguished themselves through their effectiveness, discipline and substantive contributions to parliamentary discourse.

But accountability must begin with the truth, not with a political conclusion looking for evidence.

Ghana News.title: Energy Commission, Ghana Hotels Association train Bono East hoteliers on energy efficiency
Ghana News.content:
The Energy Commission has partnered with the Ghana Hotels Association to roll out a comprehensive stakeholder engagement programme targeting hotel and hospitality facility owners and managers in the Bono East region, with a training session held in Techiman.

The initiative forms part of the Commission’s 2026 hospitality-sector sensitisation programme, which seeks to strengthen compliance with new energy efficiency regulations and build the capacity of hotel operators in energy management.

The Commission, in partnership with the Ghana Hotels Association, began the stakeholder engagement programme in 2025, covering selected regional capitals including Accra, Cape Coast, Takoradi, Ho, Koforidua, Kumasi and Sunyani.

The 2026 phase is extending the programme to other regional capitals and selected cities, including Techiman, Tamale, Bolgatanga, Damongo, Wa, Sefwi Wiawso, Goaso, Hohoe, Winneba and Nkawkaw.

The hospitality sector is considered a major consumer of electricity due to its extensive use of air conditioners, refrigerators, lighting systems, laundry equipment, kitchen appliances and other energy-intensive facilities.

Hotels spend approximately 60 to 70 per cent of their operating costs on energy and resources, making energy management a critical component of their operational expenditure.

Speaking at the stakeholders’ engagement, the Senior Manager at the Energy Efficiency Unit of the Energy Commission, Ing. John Adjei, said the move is important for two key reasons.

“One is to help them conserve energy, save money and make the hotel business profitable,” he said. “Two is to help reduce energy generation which will in turn reduce emissions from fossil fuels and reduce greenhouse gases.”

He further stated that Ghana as a country will also save money from energy generation and use it for other developmental purposes.

“Lower-priced appliances may appear attractive at the point of purchase, but they often consume more electricity and result in higher utility bills over time,” he said.

Particular attention, he noted, was being given to appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, microwave ovens and electric kettles, which can account for significant energy consumption in hotels.

He urged hotel managers and other electricity consumers to pay close attention to energy labels when purchasing appliances.

He also stressed that purchasing an energy-efficient appliance alone does not guarantee energy savings, emphasising that user behaviour and operational practices also play a critical role.

“You can buy the most efficient appliance, but the way you use it, your behaviour will indeed determine whether the product will be efficient or not,” he explained.

Some of the participants lauded the Commission for the training, emphasising the importance of the engagement. The training broadened participants’ understanding of energy management and highlighted the importance of investing in energy-efficient equipment.

The ripple effect of this training extends beyond individual hotels. By reducing the demand for electricity, the country reduces its reliance on expensive fossil fuel generation.

Hotels that invest in energy-efficient technologies and implement sound energy management systems stand to benefit from lower electricity bills, improved operational efficiency and enhanced customer comfort.

As Ghana pursues a more sustainable energy future, stakeholders believe that empowering businesses with the knowledge and tools to manage energy efficiently will not only improve profitability but also contribute significantly to national efforts to conserve energy resources and protect the environment.

Ghana News.title: GHS unveils new framework to improve Ghana’s preparedness for health emergencies
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has launched a new Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) framework to strengthen Ghana’s preparedness and response to disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies.

The framework brings together institutions, information, expertise, and resources to enable a more coordinated response when emergencies occur.

Speaking at the launch, GHS Director-General Professor Samuel Kaba Akoriyea said the PHEOC system would provide a platform for coordinated action without taking over the statutory responsibilities of other institutions.

“Importantly, the PHEOC does not replace the statutory mandates of other institutions. Rather, it provides a platform through which their mandates, capabilities, information and resources can be brought together to support coordinated public health emergency action,” he said.

Five strategic and operational documents were launched as part of the initiative.

They are the National PHEOC Strategic Plan 2026–2030, National PHEOC Handbook 2026, National PHEOC Standard Operating Procedures, Volume One, National Health Workforce Surge Strategic Plan 2026, and National Public Health Workforce Surge Management Standard Operating Procedures, Volume Two.



Professor Akoriyea said the framework would support Ghana’s implementation of the International Health Regulations 2005, address gaps identified through the Joint External Evaluation and strengthen the country’s broader health security agenda.

The GHS Director-General said the experiences of the Ebola outbreak in West Africa and the COVID-19 pandemic had demonstrated the need for countries to build emergency preparedness before crises occur.

He recalled the isolation of Liberia and Sierra Leone during the 2014 Ebola outbreak and the widespread disruption caused by COVID-19 several years later.

“Barely five years later, in 2019 and 2020, you and I witnessed our world shut down, travel limitations with numerous lockdowns, economic activities reduced to a minimum,” he said.

He said Ghana must draw lessons from those experiences to ensure that future emergencies do not overwhelm the country's response systems.

Professor Akoriyea cautioned that the effectiveness of the framework would ultimately depend on implementation rather than the documents themselves.

“The launch of these documents is not an end in itself. It marks the beginning of the next and more important phase—the phase we call implementation,” he said.

He called on stakeholders to ensure that emergency operations centres remain functional, connected and sustainable.

“Our task now is to move from documents to action, from structures to functionality, and from preparedness on paper to readiness in practice,” he added.

According to him, Ghana's emergency response system must be capable of coordinating action before, during, and after a public health emergency.

“Success is measured by our readiness to coordinate seamlessly when an emergency occurs,” he said.

Professor Akoriyea also stressed the need for public health emergency preparedness to extend beyond the health sector.

He called for stronger collaboration among government institutions, security and emergency services, academia, research institutions, civil society, the private sector and development partners.

“Public health emergency preparedness and response cannot be the responsibility of the health sector alone. It requires connected leadership and strong multisectoral coordination, timely information sharing, clear accountability and collective action,” he said.

The development of the framework involved the Ministry of Health, GHS, regional health directorates, other ministries, departments and agencies, security and emergency services, academia, professional bodies, civil society organisations and private-sector stakeholders.

Development partners, including the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the World Health Organization, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, and the Korea International Cooperation Agency, also supported the process.

Professor Akoriyea acknowledged that the newly launched documents would require continuous improvement as Ghana gains more experience in managing public health emergencies.

“Every book has Edition 1, Edition 2, etc. And it means that there will be setbacks. It’s not going to be perfect, but we are creating the platform for the next generation to take over and develop Edition 2,” he said.

He subsequently declared the national PHEOC documents officially launched and urged stakeholders to translate the framework into practical action.

The GHS believes the initiative will strengthen Ghana's ability to detect, coordinate and respond to future health emergencies while building a more resilient national health security system.

Ghana News.title: Suspected robber crashes stolen taxi into traders while fleeing mob at Ejisu
Ghana News.content:
A suspected armed robber crashed a taxi he had allegedly attempted to steal after ramming it into some shops while trying to escape a mob at the Ejisu traffic junction.

According to a witness, the suspect got into the car, a Toyota Corolla with registration number GT 1557-16, and attacked the driver, demanding he hand over the vehicle.

As he tried to get away, a group of men surrounded the car and tried to pull him out, but he reversed sharply, ploughing into the shops nearby before crashing the vehicle.

He managed to flee on foot, taking refuge inside a mobile money container as members of the public gave chase.

Police officers arrived at the scene in time and rescued the suspect from the mob before he could sustain further harm. He has since been taken into custody.

There have been no reports of injuries or casualties from the crash so far, and investigations into the incident are ongoing.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
